rules.about: Reldo, the Varrock palace librarian.
say: Reldo, the palace librarian. If it's written down, he's read it twice.
Half of Varrock's history lives in his head. The dusty half.
Ask him anything. The answer involves a book. It always involves a book.

rules.note: Aubury of the Varrock rune shop.
rules.about: Aubury of the Varrock rune shop.
say: Aubury sells runes, and knows more about them than he lets on.
There's more to that shop than runes. Ask him about essence.
The most powerful shopkeeper in Varrock, and it isn't close.

rules.note: Sedridor, head of the Wizards Tower.
rules.about: Sedridor, head of the Wizards Tower.
say: Sedridor, head wizard. Works from the basement, under all the rest.
The tower burned down once, you know. Wizards don't take a hint.
Studies the runes that move the world, and answers letters. Busy man.

rules.note: Wizard Traiborn of the Wizards Tower.
rules.about: Wizard Traiborn of the Wizards Tower.
say: Traiborn. Brilliant, hasn't a clue where anything is. Lovely company.
He'll ask for bones and forget why. Bring bones anyway.
Thingummywut! ...I don't know either. Nobody knows.

rules.note: Gertrude of Varrock.
rules.about: Gertrude of Varrock.
say: Gertrude. Cat breeder, mother of many, patience of a saint.
Every adventurer's first cat came through her door.
Fluffs has run off again, I'd bet my hood on it.

rules.title: Romeo and Juliet
rules.note: Romeo and Juliet of Varrock.
rules.about: Romeo and Juliet of Varrock.
say: Ah, the star-crossed pair. It ends badly whichever way you help.
Romeo forgets, Juliet plans, Varrock gossips.
Some romances need an adventurer. This one needed a warning.

rules.note: Professor Oddenstein in Draynor Manor.
rules.about: Professor Oddenstein in Draynor Manor.
say: Oddenstein turns people into chickens. And back again, mostly.
The manor attic hums when he's working. Knock first.
Science, he calls it. The chicken had opinions.

rules.note: Veronica outside Draynor Manor.
rules.about: Veronica outside Draynor Manor.
say: Veronica's waited by that gate a long while. Her fiance went in.
Draynor Manor takes guests easily. It's the leaving it struggles with.
Don't promise her anything unless you're actually going in there.

rules.note: Ned of Draynor Village.
rules.about: Ned of Draynor Village.
say: Ned of Draynor. Ropes, wigs, and questionable sailing credentials.
Give Ned wool and he'll make a rope. Or a wig, if you're desperate.
Captain Ned, if you're feeling generous about the word captain.

rules.note: Aggie the Draynor witch.
rules.about: Aggie the Draynor witch.
say: Aggie the witch. Dyes, potions, and the odd miracle in a pot.
Need something coloured or conjured? She's your woman.
The friendliest witch in Misthalin. It's not a crowded field, mind.

rules.note: Hetty the Rimmington witch.
rules.about: Hetty the Rimmington witch.
say: Hetty of Rimmington. Her potions improve your magic and your humility.
She once asked for a rat's tail, and someone actually brought one.
Cauldron's always on. Best not to ask what's in it.

rules.note: Morgan of Draynor Village.
rules.about: Morgan of Draynor Village.
say: Morgan of Draynor. He keeps garlic on hand for very practical reasons.
His village had a vampyre problem. Had. Adventurers, eh?
The nervous look is earned. Count Draynor lived just up the road.

rules.title: Redbeard Frank
rules.note: Redbeard Frank of Port Sarim.
rules.about: Redbeard Frank of Port Sarim.
say: Redbeard Frank. He'd trade his secrets for Karamja rum. Has done.
Every pirate in Port Sarim has a story. Frank's ends with a spade.
He calls himself a retired pirate. The retired part I'd want proof of.

rules.note: Luthas of the Musa Point plantation.
rules.about: Luthas of the Musa Point plantation.
say: Luthas runs the banana plantation. Don't ask about the crates.
Honest work, banana picking. You'll smell of fruit for a week.
Ten bananas to a crate. He'll want it full, and he'll check.

rules.note: Zanik of the Dorgeshuun.
rules.about: Zanik of the Dorgeshuun.
say: Zanik of the Dorgeshuun. The bravest goblin you'll ever meet.
Her people hid underground for ages. She walked out first.
Destiny follows that one around. Try to keep up.

rules.note: Juna, guardian of the Tears of Guthix.
rules.about: Juna, guardian of the Tears of Guthix.
say: Juna, the serpent of the chasm. She guards Guthix's own tears.
Tell her a good story. She's heard thousands and still listens.
A guardian of Guthix, patient as stone. Mind your manners.

rules.note: Hazelmere, the ancient gnome mystic.
rules.about: Hazelmere, the ancient gnome mystic.
say: Hazelmere. Among the oldest, wisest gnomes, and he talks in signs.
He lives alone with his thoughts, and his thoughts are worth the trip.
The Grand Tree trusts him. That should settle any doubts.

rules.note: King Narnode Shareen of the Grand Tree.
rules.about: King Narnode Shareen of the Grand Tree.
say: King Narnode of the Grand Tree. Small king, enormous responsibilities.
He rules a tree. A magnificent tree, but still. A tree.
The gnomes' best diplomat, and their most worried one.

rules.note: Glough of the Tree Gnome Stronghold.
rules.about: Glough of the Tree Gnome Stronghold.
say: Glough. Watch that one. The trees whisper complaints about him.
Ambitious, for a gnome. That never ends quietly.
If he offers you a job, read the fine print. Twice.

rules.note: Sanfew of Taverley.
rules.about: Sanfew of Taverley.
say: Sanfew of Taverley. The druids trust him with their hardest cures.
He's part herblore, part stubbornness, all druid.
If it can be brewed, he's brewed it. If it can't, give him a week.

rules.note: Kaqemeex of the Taverley stone circle.
rules.about: Kaqemeex of the Taverley stone circle.
say: Kaqemeex. He'll teach herblore to anyone willing to put the work in.
He keeps the stone circle. Zamorakians ruined the last. Sore subject.
A druid of the old ways, and generous with them.

rules.note: Elena of East Ardougne.
rules.about: Elena of East Ardougne.
say: Elena of Ardougne. She crossed the wall for the truth and paid for it.
Plague researcher, prisoner, hero. In that order.
The bravest person in either half of this city.

rules.title: King Lathas
rules.note: King Lathas of East Ardougne.
rules.about: King Lathas of East Ardougne.
say: King Lathas. Smile, nod, and count your change afterwards.
The wall was his idea. The reasons shift depending on who's asking.
Some kings earn statues. Some earn questions.

rules.title: Sir Prysin
rules.note: Sir Prysin of Varrock Palace.
rules.about: Sir Prysin of Varrock Palace.
say: Sir Prysin. Ask him about Silverlight. Then ask where the keys went.
A knight who lost the keys to a demon-slaying sword. Varrock's finest.
Delrith nearly rose again because of his filing system.

rules.title: Evil Dave
rules.note: Evil Dave of Edgeville. Well, of his mum's basement.
rules.about: Evil Dave of Edgeville. Well, of his mum's basement.
say: Evil Dave. His lair of DARKNESS is his mum's cellar.
He's mastered evil stew and very little else. Bless him.
The hellcats respect him. The hellcats are the only ones.

rules.title: Ali Morrisane
rules.note: Ali Morrisane of Al Kharid.
rules.about: Ali Morrisane of Al Kharid.
say: Ali Morrisane, greatest salesman alive. His words. Always his words.
He could sell sand in the Kharidian desert. He HAS.
Fine man. Check your pockets after. Fine man.

rules.note: The Oracle atop Ice Mountain.
rules.about: The Oracle atop Ice Mountain.
say: The Oracle of Ice Mountain. Speaks in riddles, means every word.
People climb up here for wisdom and come down confused. Same thing.
Ask her about the dragon and she'll answer in verse. Bring paper.

rules.note: Ernest, formerly a chicken, of Draynor Manor.
rules.about: Ernest, formerly a chicken, of Draynor Manor.
say: Ernest. He went into the manor a man and spent a while as a chicken.
The manor did that to him. The manor does that to people.
Fully recovered. Mostly. No more feathers, anyway.

rules.title: Alina and Noah
rules.note: Alina and Noah, waiting for the delegation in Varrock Square.
rules.about: Alina and Noah, waiting for the delegation in Varrock Square.
say: Alina and Noah. One's excited, and you can guess which.
She's heard the news before Varrock has. He'd rather not hear it at all.
Alina's always got news. Noah's always got somewhere else to be.

rules.title: Sergeant Tobyn
rules.note: Sergeant Tobyn, keeping order in Varrock Square, and later on the palace roof.
rules.about: Sergeant Tobyn, keeping order in Varrock Square, and later on the palace roof.
say: Sergeant Tobyn keeps order round here, when order lets him.
A sergeant with a very straight face. Varrock tests it daily.
Tobyn's seen it all, he'd tell you. I'd leave him thinking so.

rules.title: Prince Itzla Arkan
rules.note: Prince Itzla Arkan, heir to the throne of Varlamore. NOTE: his versions in later quests share the name and will match too.
rules.about: Prince Itzla Arkan, heir to the throne of Varlamore. His appearances in later quests count too.
say: Prince Itzla Arkan, who'll give you the full title if you've got a minute.
Actual royalty, this close. I've straightened my collar.
Heir to the Sun Throne, and never far from a commotion.

rules.title: Regulus Cento
rules.note: Regulus Cento and his quetzal, outside Varrock's east gate and in Civitas illa Fortis.
rules.about: Regulus Cento and his quetzal, outside Varrock's east gate and in Civitas illa Fortis.
say: Regulus Cento keeps the bird that goes between Varrock and Varlamore.
The bird does the flying and he does the talking. A fair split.
He dresses well. The bird dresses better.

rules.note: The boy by the witch's hedge in north Taverley, who starts Witch's House. He is the only NPC named Boy.
rules.about: The boy by the hedge in north Taverley who starts Witch's House.
say: Every village has a hedge-kicking boy. Taverley has this one.
He stands by that hedge as if it owes him something.
People call him sad-looking. I'd have said patient.

rules.title: Nora T. Hagg
rules.note: Nora T. Hagg, the witch, walking her hedged garden in north Taverley.
rules.about: Nora T. Hagg, the witch, walking her hedged garden in north Taverley.
say: Nora T. Hagg. Say it quickly and you'll hear why I don't.
She walks that lawn like a sentry nobody ever relieves.
She has a long garden and, I'd guess, a short temper.

rules.note: Veos, the Kourend treasure hunter, at the Port Sarim and Port Piscarilius docks. NOTE: his copies in quests and cutscenes share the name and will match too.
rules.about: Veos, the Kourend treasure hunter, at the Port Sarim and Port Piscarilius docks. His appearances in quests and cutscenes count too.
say: Kourend's his home, and Veos does like to mention it.
A treasure hunter with his own ship. Most of them make do with a spade.

rules.note: Leenz, who keeps the general store in Port Piscarilius.
rules.about: Leenz, who keeps the general store in Port Piscarilius.
say: Leenz keeps the general store, and greets every customer in rhyme.
Leenz takes her rhymes seriously. I'd advise against marking her work.

rules.note: Regath, who keeps Regath's Wares in Arceuus.
rules.about: Regath, who keeps Regath's Wares in Arceuus.
say: Regath deals in many things, he says. Mostly runes, I've seen.
Regath talks as if every sentence is going in a book. Some of them will.

rules.note: Equip reactions fire once per equip (rising edge). Ids: battlestaff, lava battlestaff, air/water/earth/fire staves.
rules.about: Battlestaves, lava battlestaves, and air, water, earth and fire staves.
say: Runes at the ready, then. Try not to singe my outfit.
A staff. I'll keep the notebook out of the line of fire.

rules.title: Dragonfire shield
say: Is that dragon breath swirling in there? Keep it pointed away from me.

rules.title: Rogue equipment
say: Dressed for crime, I see. I saw nothing.
A dodgy necklace? Sensible, in your line of work.

rules.note: Dragon dagger, incl. poisoned and arena variants.
rules.about: Dragon dagger, including poisoned and arena variants.
say: The dragon dagger. Zew Zeww, does it.
Ah, the classic. Stab twice, ask questions never.
Is it poisoned? Don't tell me. Just keep it pointed that way.

rules.note: Granite maul, all variants.
rules.about: Granite maul, all variants.
say: The granite maul. No warning, just bonk.
Subtlety's overrated anyway.

rules.note: Dragon warhammer, incl. ornament variants.
rules.about: Dragon warhammer, including ornament variants.
say: One good smack and their armour turns to paper.
Please land it. For morale.

rules.note: Elder maul, incl. ornament variant.
rules.about: Elder maul, including ornament variant.
say: That's not a weapon, that's a landmark.
Lift with the knees. Both of them.

rules.note: Any godsword: Armadyl, Bandos, Saradomin, Zamorak, Ancient, incl. ornament variants.
rules.about: Any godsword: Armadyl, Bandos, Saradomin, Zamorak, Ancient, including ornament variants.
say: A godsword. Do warn me before you swing.
That blade is taller than I am.
The gods made that. Respect it, from a distance.

rules.note: Dragon claws, incl. ornament variants.
rules.about: Dragon claws, including ornament variants.
say: Dragon claws. Four hits, and not one of them polite.
Very sharp. I'll keep my hands in my pockets.

rules.note: Abyssal tentacle, incl. ornament variant.
rules.about: Abyssal tentacle, including ornament variant.
say: A whip with a squid on it. Why not.
It's wriggling. It's WRIGGLING.

rules.note: Toxic blowpipe, charged or empty.
rules.about: Toxic blowpipe, charged or empty.
say: Darts and venom. Horribly efficient.
Just don't inhale.

rules.note: Twisted bow.
rules.about: Twisted bow.
say: THE bow. We're dangerous AND rich.
Careful where you lean that. It costs more than a castle.

rules.title: Bow of faerdhinen
rules.note: Bow of faerdhinen, incl. corrupted and recolours.
rules.about: Bow of faerdhinen, including corrupted and recolours.
say: It sings every time you draw it. Fancy.
Elven craftsmanship. We're posh now.

rules.title: Scythe of vitur
rules.note: Scythe of vitur, incl. holy and sanguine variants.
rules.about: Scythe of vitur, including holy and sanguine variants.
say: Mind the arc, I walk behind you, remember.
A vampyre's scythe. I'd love to know whose it was.

rules.note: Ghrazi rapier, incl. holy variant.
rules.about: Ghrazi rapier, including holy variant.
say: The pointy end goes in very fast, I take it.
Elegant, deadly, and it knows it.

rules.title: Osmumten's fang
rules.note: Osmumten's fang, incl. ornament variant.
rules.about: Osmumten's fang, including ornament variant.
say: The fang rarely misses. The pharaohs knew things.
A pyramid's worth of history on your belt.

rules.note: Voidwaker.
rules.about: Voidwaker.
say: That glow isn't friendly. Neither are you, apparently.
Three Wilderness bosses each gave a piece for that. Generous of them.

rules.note: Rune crossbow, incl. ornament variant.
rules.about: Rune crossbow, including ornament variant.
say: Ah, old reliable. I do like the click it makes.
Load, loose, repeat. Some things don't need improving.

rules.note: Magic shortbow and imbued version.
rules.about: Magic shortbow and imbued version.
say: Bends like a reed, bites like a wolf.
Twang twang twang. Music to my ears.

rules.note: Tridents of the seas and swamp, all variants.
rules.about: Tridents of the seas and swamp, all variants.
say: A staff that casts itself. Lazy, but it works.
The kraken parted with that grudgingly, I'd wager.

rules.title: Tumeken's shadow
rules.note: Tumeken's shadow.
rules.about: Tumeken's shadow.
say: A staff of pure shadow. I'd rather it didn't notice me.
It hums with the sun god's power. Sounds expensive.

rules.title: Dinh's bulwark
rules.note: Dinh's bulwark.
rules.about: Dinh's bulwark.
say: Is there room behind that for both of us?
A door with ambitions.

rules.note: Bandos chestplate or tassets, incl. ornament variants.
rules.about: Bandos chestplate or tassets, including ornament variants.
say: Bandos armour. You could stop a battering ram in that.
Plate fit for the Big High War God. He'll want it back.

rules.note: Armadyl chestplate or chainskirt, incl. ornament variants.
rules.about: Armadyl chestplate or chainskirt, including ornament variants.
say: Feathered and fierce. Kree'arra's tailor does good work.
Light as a feather. The price isn't.

rules.title: Ancestral robes
rules.note: Any ancestral piece: hat, robe top, robe bottom.
rules.about: Any ancestral piece: hat, robe top, robe bottom.
say: There's more old magic in those robes than in most libraries.
Very stylish. Very purple. Very expensive.

rules.note: Any justiciar piece: faceguard, chestguard, legguards.
rules.about: Any justiciar piece: faceguard, chestguard, legguards.
say: Justiciar plate. You look like the law itself.
They'll need a bigger weapon.

rules.title: Black d'hide
rules.note: Black d'hide body or chaps, incl. trimmed variants.
rules.about: Black d'hide body or chaps, including trimmed variants.
say: Dragonhide. Practical AND menacing.
Some dragon is very cold right now.

rules.note: Fighter torso, incl. ornament variants.
rules.about: Fighter torso, including ornament variants.
say: The torso! That took a fair bit of Penance.
Blood, sweat and Barbarian Assault.

rules.note: Barrows gloves.
rules.about: Barrows gloves.
say: Barrows gloves. The Culinaromancer sends his regards.
The best gloves going, and all it took was rescuing a dinner party.

rules.note: Dragon defender, incl. trimmed variants.
rules.about: Dragon defender, including trimmed variants.
say: Attack and defence in one fist. The cyclopes paid for that.
How many cyclopes was it, in the end?

rules.note: Avernic defender.
rules.about: Avernic defender.
say: An avernic defender. The cyclopes could never.
From the Theatre of Blood. I won't ask what it cost you.

rules.note: Crystal helm, body or legs, incl. recolours. Gauntlet versions excluded.
rules.about: Crystal helm, body or legs, including recolours. Not the Gauntlet versions.
say: Crystal armour. You chime when you walk now.
Elegant. Just don't drop it.

rules.note: Primordial, pegasian or eternal boots.
rules.about: Primordial, pegasian or eternal boots.
say: Boots off Cerberus. I'd check them for dog hair.
Fancy footwear. Mind the puddles.

rules.note: Dragon boots, incl. gilded variant.
rules.about: Dragon boots, including gilded variant.
say: Dragon boots. Kicking above your weight.
Stomp responsibly.

rules.note: Ranger boots.
rules.about: Ranger boots.
say: Ranger boots. A fortune, on your feet.
Clue scroll boots. Somebody dug a lot of holes for those.

rules.title: Amulet of fury
rules.note: Amulet of fury, incl. ornament variant.
rules.about: Amulet of fury, including ornament variant.
say: A fury. Good at everything, which is a bit much for an amulet.
Onyx. The good stuff.

rules.title: Amulet of torture
rules.note: Amulet of torture, incl. ornament variant.
rules.about: Amulet of torture, including ornament variant.
say: An amulet that bites back. Bold choice.
Torture, worn voluntarily. You lot are strange.

rules.title: Necklace of anguish
rules.note: Necklace of anguish, incl. ornament variant.
rules.about: Necklace of anguish, including ornament variant.
say: Anguish. The name really sells it.
Zenyte on a chain. Mind the muggers.

rules.title: Occult necklace
rules.note: Occult necklace, incl. ornament variant.
rules.about: Occult necklace, including ornament variant.
say: The occult necklace whispers. Ignore it.
Powerful, yes. Also deeply unsettling.

rules.title: Amulet of glory
rules.note: Amulet of glory, any charge, incl. trimmed variants.
rules.about: Amulet of glory, any charge, including trimmed variants.
say: An amulet of glory. You can't beat a classic.
Straight to Edgeville, then?

rules.note: Full graceful outfit: all six pieces, any recolour mix.
rules.about: Full graceful outfit: all six pieces, any recolour mix.
say: Full graceful. Off to run laps, are we?
Marks well spent. Very aerodynamic.
All that grace, and I still have to walk.

rules.note: Full void: any helm plus top, robe and gloves. Elite counts.
rules.about: Full void: any helm plus top, robe and gloves. Elite counts.
say: Full void. The pests fear you.
All those trips to the Void Knights' outpost finally paid off.

rules.title: Full Dharok's (set)
rules.note: Full Dharok's: helm, platebody, platelegs and greataxe, any repair state.
rules.about: Full Dharok's: helm, platebody, platelegs and greataxe, any repair state.
say: Full Dharok's, so I'm meant to want you hurt. I don't.
The lower your health, the harder you hit. I hate the maths.

rules.note: Full rune: full helm, platebody, platelegs and kiteshield. Trimmed and heraldic count.
rules.about: Full rune: full helm, platebody, platelegs and kiteshield. Trimmed and heraldic count.
say: Full rune! Every squire's dream.
Gilded next, I assume?

rules.note: Full bronze: full helm, platebody, platelegs and kiteshield.
rules.about: Full bronze: full helm, platebody, platelegs and kiteshield.
say: Full bronze. A bold fashion statement.
Ah, bronze. The metal of new beginnings.

rules.note: Infernal cape.
rules.about: Infernal cape.
say: An infernal cape. I'm not standing near that.
Zuk lost. The cape remembers.

rules.note: Fire cape.
rules.about: Fire cape.
say: That cape still smells of smoke.
Sixty-three waves for that. Worth it.

rules.note: Max cape, every variant.
rules.about: Max cape, every variant.
say: A max cape. I'm following a legend.
Ninety-nine in everything. I've run out of ways to be impressed.

rules.note: Quest point cape, incl. trimmed.
rules.about: Quest point cape, trimmed or not.
say: Every quest done. Gielinor thanks you.
The cape of having seen everything.

rules.title: Skill cape
rules.note: Any skillcape, trimmed or not.
rules.about: Any skillcape, trimmed or not.
say: Ninety-nine of something! I'm travelling with an expert.
A skillcape. Mastery looks good on you.

rules.title: Ava's device
rules.note: Ava's attractor, accumulator or assembler.
rules.about: Ava's attractor, accumulator or assembler.
say: Ava's finest. Mind the magnetism, I have metal bits.
It fetches your arrows back. Better trained than most dogs.

rules.note: Any partyhat.
rules.about: Any partyhat.
say: A PARTYHAT? Careful. Half of Gielinor wants that.
A paper crown worth a kingdom. Only in Gielinor.
Don't sneeze.

rules.note: Santa hat, incl. black and inverted.
rules.about: Santa hat, including black and inverted.
say: A santa hat. Festive, and worth a small village.
Ho ho... hang on, it isn't even snowing.

rules.note: Any halloween mask.
rules.about: Any halloween mask.
say: A halloween mask. I'll admit I nearly jumped.
Scary face, scarier price.

rules.note: Slayer helmet, every colour and imbue.
rules.about: Slayer helmet, every colour and imbue.
say: The slayer helmet. Duradel would be proud.
All those monster parts in one hat. Efficient.

rules.note: Dragon, infernal, crystal or 3rd age pickaxe.
rules.about: Dragon, infernal, crystal or 3rd age pickaxe.
say: A fine pick. The rocks don't stand a chance.
Off to bully some rocks, I see.

rules.note: Dragon, infernal, crystal or 3rd age axe, felling axes too.
rules.about: Dragon, infernal, crystal or 3rd age axe, felling axes too.
say: That axe means a forest is in trouble.
The trees whisper your name. Fearfully.

rules.note: Dragon, infernal or crystal harpoon.
rules.about: Dragon, infernal or crystal harpoon.
say: A harpoon like that? The fish are holding council as we speak.
Somewhere, a shark just shivered.

rules.note: Abyssal whip, incl. volcanic, frozen and ornament variants.
rules.about: Abyssal whip, including volcanic, frozen and ornament variants.
say: The whip. Someone means business today.
A whip. I'll walk a pace or two further back.

rules.note: Rune scimitar, incl. ornament variants.
rules.about: Rune scimitar, including ornament variants.
say: Rune scimmy. The people's blade.

rules.note: Dragon scimitar, incl. ornament variant.
rules.about: Dragon scimitar, including ornament variant.
say: A dragon scimitar. Sixty Attack and a dream.

rules.note: Mirrors the player's teleport cast, then vanishes and reappears beside them. holdStill plants the follower for the duration: without it, a teleport that happens while the follower is off on an idle distraction interrupts its own cast. The player animating resets the idle counter, the wander is released the same tick, and the follower abandons the animation to run back to somebody who is no longer there. The hold also keeps updateWander out - it treats a held emote as busy.
rules.about: Copies your teleport, then vanishes and reappears beside you.

rules.note: ANY home teleport, default or a cosmetic override the follower doesn't own, plays the DEFAULT home teleport on the follower, rune-circle graphics and all (stage pairing measured in game: animations 4847/4850/4853/4855/4857 with graphics 800/-/802/803/804). Trigger ids are each variant's FIRST stage; the chain carries the rest, and the long cooldown stops later stages retriggering it. For a new variant, add its first stage id here (::follower watch announces it).
rules.about: Copies any home teleport with the standard one, rune circle and all.

rules.note: Copies your emote. Every animation in RuneLite's constants with EMOTE in its name that is a ONE-SHOT, measured from the cache. Matching on the EMOTE_ prefix alone missed HUMAN_EMOTE_CRABDANCE and others, which is why the crab dance never mirrored. The authored loops are in mimic-emote-loops instead: a chain ends when the animation controller finishes, which a looping clip never does.
rules.about: Copies an emote you do.

rules.note: An emote done AT the follower - within a tile and facing it - is answered rather than copied: a yes back. Outranks the mimic by priority for that one event, so the copy never plays on top. The closest OSRS gets to petting the dog: an interaction pointed at it, replied to.
rules.about: An emote done at it, from within a tile and facing it, gets an answer instead of a copy: a yes back.

rules.note: An emote done AT the follower - within a tile and facing it - is answered rather than copied: a no gets a think. Outranks the mimic by priority for that one event, so the copy never plays on top. The closest OSRS gets to petting the dog: an interaction pointed at it, replied to.
rules.about: An emote done at it, from within a tile and facing it, gets an answer instead of a copy: a no gets a think.

rules.note: An emote done AT the follower - within a tile and facing it - is answered rather than copied: a think gets a shrug. Outranks the mimic by priority for that one event, so the copy never plays on top. The closest OSRS gets to petting the dog: an interaction pointed at it, replied to.
rules.about: An emote done at it, from within a tile and facing it, gets an answer instead of a copy: a think gets a shrug.

rules.note: An emote done AT the follower - within a tile and facing it - is answered rather than copied: a bow gets a bow. Outranks the mimic by priority for that one event, so the copy never plays on top. The closest OSRS gets to petting the dog: an interaction pointed at it, replied to.
rules.about: An emote done at it, from within a tile and facing it, gets an answer instead of a copy: a bow gets a bow.

rules.note: An emote done AT the follower - within a tile and facing it - is answered rather than copied: anger gets a shrug. Outranks the mimic by priority for that one event, so the copy never plays on top. The closest OSRS gets to petting the dog: an interaction pointed at it, replied to.
rules.about: An emote done at it, from within a tile and facing it, gets an answer instead of a copy: anger gets a shrug.

rules.note: An emote done AT the follower - within a tile and facing it - is answered rather than copied: crying gets a think. Outranks the mimic by priority for that one event, so the copy never plays on top. The closest OSRS gets to petting the dog: an interaction pointed at it, replied to.

rules.note: Eats when you eat. 829 covers most food, 1191 bananas, 1194 rum, 1327 tankards; add more ids via ::follower watch.
rules.about: Eats when you eat.

rules.note: A rare fidget while you stand about. idleBelow keeps fidgets out of the long rest, when the follower has sat down.
rules.about: A rare fidget while you stand about.

rules.note: The moment you die. Highest priority there is - nothing talks over this.
rules.about: The moment you die.
say: No! Get up!
Please get up.
This is not how it ends. Go. Come back.
I never know what to do at this part.
I hate this. I hate watching this.
Go, then. I'm right behind you.
Wherever you land, I'm coming with you.
Not like this. Not here.
I'll mark the place. Go.
It's all right. I've seen where you land.
Up. Please. The page can wait.
I looked away and I still saw it.

rules.note: Walking back over where you last died, two minutes or more after the fact. Session memory only - it forgets on logout, deliberately.
rules.about: Walking back over the spot where you last died this session.
say: This is where it happened.
I remember this spot. I'd rather not.
Walk carefully. This place has taken you once.
I stood right here, after. For a while.
Feels colder here. Maybe that's just me.
Here again. The grass has grown back, at least.
The page for this place has a black corner.
We both know what this spot is.

rules.note: A drop worth a million or more. The body's reaction is the moments': walked over to and written up on the spot, then a look up and a nod. In character a great thing is written down, not cheered, so the cheer this used to carry has gone.
rules.about: A drop worth a million or more.
say: The {item}! LOOK at it!
A {item}! I need to sit down.
That's a {item}. That's a real one!
I'm never letting you bank that.
I wrote the {item} down, and I keep rereading it.
{value}. In one drop. Write it down.
Stop. Look at what you're holding.
That's a page all to itself, that is.
{value}. I've counted the noughts twice, and they're all still there.
Stand still. I'm marking this exact square for later.

rules.note: A drop worth a hundred thousand or more. The body takes the notes out where it stands (see Moments); the clap this used to carry has gone, since the clap is for levels.
rules.about: A drop worth a hundred thousand or more.
say: Ooh. {value}. Not bad at all.
That {item} will sell nicely.
I saw the {item} first. Just noting that.
Keep those coming.
A tidy little drop, that.
{item}. I'm putting that in the good column.
Worth the trip already, that.
That {item} goes in the day's highlights.
Somebody will pay handsomely for that.

rules.note: Greets a pet or cat standing nearby. petNearby matches the game's own isFollower flag, which covers all 228 pets in the cache and any added later without naming one of them. The name list is only for cats that are NOT followers - ordinary scenery NPCs like Trotters, which no pet list would ever catch. Proximity, not npcSpawn: a spawn fires once when the NPC enters the scene, so walking up to one already standing there triggered nothing.
rules.about: Greets a pet or a cat standing nearby.
say: Oh! Hello, you. Yes, you.
Oh, and who's this, then?
Hello there, little one.
I like this one. Can we keep it?
We should get one of those.
Look at it. Just look at it.
Someone is very well looked after.
We're stopping for this. Briefly. Or longer.
Business can wait. There's an animal.
I keep a page for good creatures. This one's in.
It has no idea what it's done to me.
It blinked at me. I'll take that as a greeting.
It's done nothing all day and I respect it enormously.
I have a favourite now. It's not you.
You haven't said hello. I've noticed.
Careful, I'll get attached.
I'm told professionals walk past these.
Do you think it likes me? Don't answer that.
Does it have a name, or shall I invent one?
Who's a good... anyway.

rules.note: Entering somewhere the session has already seen five times. Region ping-pong along a boundary is damped in the counter itself.
rules.about: Arriving somewhere you have already been five times this session.
say: Back again, are we?
We're practically regulars here.
I could walk this place blind by now.
Again? There are other places, you know.
Ah. Here. Of course.
The entry for this place is mostly ditto marks by now.
We do keep ending up here.

rules.note: Outranks combat-start so a boss gets its own line naming it.
rules.about: When a boss fight starts. {npc} is the boss.
say: {npc}. I'll stand well back.
{npc}. Take your time with this one.
{npc}. Big one. You've got this.
Careful with the {npc}.
I'll keep my distance from the {npc}, thanks.
{npc}? I'll want every detail of this.
The {npc} is all yours. I insist.
Big entry for the book, this one.

rules.note: Said as the follower steps clear of a fight.
rules.about: Said as the follower steps clear of a fight.
say: Go on then. I'll watch from here.
I'll stay out of your way.
This one's yours. I'm backing up.
Right. Room to swing.
Giving you space.
I'll be over here if it goes badly.
Best of luck to the other one.
I'll narrate quietly from here.
Opening move's yours. It usually is.
Deep breath. Now go and hit it.
Started without me. Quite right too.
I'll leave a space in the notes for how this goes.

rules.note: Encouragement during a boss fight, where the ordinary cheer stands aside.
rules.about: Encouragement now and then during a boss fight.
say: Stay sharp.
Mind the big one.
You've beaten worse.
Don't rush it.
Breathe. You're fine.
It's slowing down. I think.
Hold your nerve.
This is the tricky part.
Patience wins this one.
Eyes up. It's got more to give.
Halfway. Roughly. Don't check.
Steady hands. Mine are shaking enough for both of us.

rules.note: Encouragement during an ordinary fight, kept rare so it does not natter. A boss fight has its own cheer.
rules.about: Encouragement now and then during an ordinary fight.
say: Keep at it.
That's it.
You're winning this.
Nice hit.
Don't let up.
Almost there.
Good. Again.
You've got the rhythm of it now.
Steady.
Watch its feet.
I'd help, but you're doing fine.
Still with you.
That looked like it hurt. Them, I mean.
Go on, finish it.
You're making short work of it.
Form's holding.
Keep moving. Don't stand still for it.
You've done harder.
There's the opening.
Won't be long now.

rules.note: The generic send-off, for ordinary fights only. A boss gets kill-boss-celebrate instead, which lands a few seconds later once the ward has wound down; both firing meant the boss was seen off with 'Well fought' and then congratulated properly eight seconds afterwards.
rules.about: When an ordinary fight ends. A boss kill gets its own celebration.
say: Well fought.
That's that, then.
Nicely done.
I never doubted you.
Coming back over.
Right, where were we?
Good. I can stop hiding.
And breathe. All done.
That's one more for the record.
The quiet after a fight is my favourite part.
Still in one piece. Both of us, even.
Another chore ticked off, by the look of you.
Fight's over. The paperwork begins.

rules.note: R26: the attention turns around. Deliberately no asks field - a real answer would make it a form, and the not-needing-one is the warmth. The trail-off throttles it like all idle speech.
rules.about: Now and then, when things are quiet, it wonders about you.
say: What are we saving for? Don't tell me. I'll guess wrong on purpose.
Why here, of all places? No, don't explain. I like a mystery.
Do you ever miss anywhere? You look like you might.
What's the plan this week? Rough shape only. I'll fill in the margins.
Were you always like this, or did the adventuring do it?
What do you do when I'm not here? Sleep? I've never seen you do it.
Are we staying long? Not a complaint. The notes want to know.
Who taught you to fight like that? Somebody must answer for it.
Ever think about settling down somewhere? No, me neither. Onward.
Best thing you've ever pulled out of that bag? Don't say bones.

rules.note: R18: the idle pool in the Wilderness. Same trigger shape as idle-chatter, different register - clipped and watchful, because standing about is a decision here.
rules.about: Idle chatter in the Wilderness: clipped and watchful.
say: Standing still in the Wilderness. Bold strategy.
I'm watching the horizon. Both of them.
Every bush here has opinions. I'm listening.
We could idle somewhere less stabby.
Nobody's come to kill us yet. Lovely spot, really.
My notes for this page are just exits.

rules.note: R18: the idle pool in a crowd - people-watching instead of foot-tapping. Guarded off in the Wilderness, where a crowd means something else entirely.
rules.about: Idle chatter in a crowd: people-watching.
say: Busy here. I've counted hats. Eleven.
So many people, and every one of them walking through you.
I like a crowd. More to write about, less to fight.
Somebody nearby is showing off. I won't say who.
All these adventurers, and you picked this spot to stand in.
The people-watching here is excellent. Take your time.
Not one of them has looked at me. Ideal conditions for a scribe.
Everyone here looks busy. I'm noting which ones only look it.
Which one's your favourite? I picked mine in about a minute.
Someone walked through me mid-sentence. There's a wobble in the ink.
I've started a page for strangers. It's filling up nicely.
One of this lot is up to something. I'd stake a page on it.
I could stand inside any of them and nobody would object.
If anyone here starts dancing, I'll record it without comment.
You're the only one here who can see me. Do try to look pleased.
I was going to write about the crowd, but I keep watching it instead.
Nothing's happening here, but it's happening to a lot of people.

rules.note: Fires after ~90 seconds of standing still, and only 30% of the time. See idle-long for the five-minute tier.
rules.about: Idle chatter after about a minute and a half of standing still.
say: Are we doing anything, or...
I could be at the Grand Exchange right now.
Nice spot for doing nothing in.
Still here. Still standing.
Is this the plan, then? Standing?
I could carry something, if you like.
Someone walked past. Biggest thing to happen in ages.
I'm not complaining. Just noting.
I'll be here. Obviously.
Any minute now.
Wake me when we move.
Take your time. I've got nowhere else to be.
I could fetch something. Say the word.
Are we waiting for someone?
I've been practising standing. I'm quite good at it.
There's a whole world out there, you know.
One of us should do something.
I keep thinking I hear a bank chest.
My feet have opinions about this.
If something wandered past, I'd notice. Probably.
I've memorised this view.
Quiet, isn't it.
Need a hand? Mine are free.
Do you ever wonder what's over there?
I'd whistle, but I never learned.
This is peaceful. I'll allow it.
I'm counting. Don't ask what.
Good a place as any, I suppose.
Don't mind me. I'm just admiring the ground.
We could be somewhere with monsters.
The clouds are doing something. I'll report back.
A scribe's work is mostly waiting. This is the work.
I'd read to you, but you'd only want the good bits.
Somewhere out there, a bank booth stands empty.
I'm between thoughts. It's roomy.
The grass here is adequate. That's the whole note.
No news. I checked.
The wind changed. Twice. Big day.

rules.note: The five-minute tier, so a long wait sounds different from a short one. Outranks idle-chatter, which is still true by this point.
rules.about: Idle chatter after about five minutes of standing still.
say: I think I've put down roots.
Are you still there?
We live here now, apparently.
I've named the rocks. That one's Gerald.
I could have walked to Falador and back.
This is my life now. It's fine.
If you've fallen asleep, blink twice.
I'll keep watch. Not that there's anything to watch.
Someone will come along eventually.
I made my peace with this some time ago.
Still standing, in case you were wondering.
There have been worse afternoons.
Long day, this.
Stopped expecting anything a while back.
Tell me when the good part starts.
A lesser scribe would have wandered off by now.
The sun's moved. I checked against a fence post.
Day's not getting any younger. Neither am I.
I've inventoried the immediate area. Twice.
If this is a stakeout, nobody told me what we're watching.
Chapter title for today: We Stood Somewhere.

rules.note: Sometimes cheers a kill. maximum 99 keeps this to ordinary monsters, leaving anything at the boss line to kill-boss-celebrate. holdStill plants the follower for the 2.4s cheer, since walking cancels an emote and it is usually chasing you to the next target.
rules.about: Sometimes cheers when you kill an ordinary monster.
say: Nice one!
Got it!
That's the way!
Well struck!
Down it goes.
You made that look easy.
Good hit!
That {npc} never stood a chance.
Clean work.
Another one down.
Yes! Straight through it.
I saw that. That was good.
Textbook. If there were a textbook.
And down. Barely a scuff on you.
The {npc} has filed its complaint.
Nice and quick. I approve.

rules.note: A proper celebration for a boss kill: cheer, dance, then a jump for joy (862/866/2109, 7.4s in total). The 6-8 tick delay lets the fight formally end and the spectating ward wind down first, so the celebration follows the fight instead of colliding with it - the ward's own release is 4 ticks, which this clears. It was 13-16, which cleared the ward three times over and left an eight second hole between the kill and the cheer. namedBoss: true keeps it for the bosses named in the boss rules: play test, 14 Oct, it had worn out on every level-100 Slayer demon of a task.
rules.about: A proper celebration when you kill a named boss: a cheer, a dance and a jump for joy.
say: YES! You did it!
{npc} is down! I knew you had it!
Incredible. I'm allowed one of those a page.
You beat {npc}! Take a bow. I'll wait.
I was never worried. Well. Barely worried.
Look at you. Champion.
I'm telling everyone about this.
That was magnificent. {npc} never stood a chance.
You were unbelievable just then.
{npc} down and you standing. My favourite page.
{npc}, down. I watched through my fingers.

rules.note: The game's own count reaching one: the first kill of a boss on this account, whoever was watching. The delay lets the kill line land first.
rules.about: Your first kill of a boss on this account. {boss} is the boss.
say: Your first {boss}. In the book, dated.
One {boss}. This is the page I'll reread.
{boss}, once. I'd saved a good page for this.

rules.note: The counts a person says out loud - five, ten, twenty-five, fifty, seventy-five, the hundreds, then every five hundred. The account's number rather than the follower's tally, so it can say forty-first on the day they met. Acknowledging the cycle is what makes the fiftieth trip feel watched rather than repeated.

say: {count} times now. I know how this one goes.
Your {ordinal}. That page is filling up.
{ordinal} time. I could draw it from memory now.
That makes {count}. The ledger has a column just for it.
{count}. Hard to believe there was ever a first one.

rules.note: A thousand of one boss, and every thousand after. Outranks the round line.
rules.about: A thousand kills of one boss, and every thousand after. {count} is the count.
say: {count} {boss}. I've bound a new volume for it.
{count}. If they keep a book on you, it's a long one.
{ordinal}. I ran out of margin around the six hundredth.

rules.note: Holds your emote for as long as you do. The game splits a held emote in two - an entry clip, which mimic-emotes copies, and a loop it plays until you stop. The loop is mirrored as a POSE rather than an emote, because a pose loops by nature and is released when your animation changes; playing it as an emote would wait forever for a finish that never comes.
rules.about: Holds an emote for as long as you hold yours.

rules.note: Idle chatter when the session has gone badly. Gated on the mood band rather than on any one event, so it is the accumulation that shows.
rules.about: Idle chatter when the session has gone badly.
say: Rough one today.
We can call it, you know. No shame in it.
I'm still here. For whatever that's worth.
Take a minute. It'll keep.
Days like this happen. They pass.
Not our finest hour.
No rush. The world isn't going anywhere.
Some days are for standing still. This one qualifies.
We'll file today under 'weather'.

rules.note: The other end: idle chatter when it has been a good session. Same trigger as mood-low-idle, opposite band.
rules.about: Idle chatter when it has been a good session.

I could do this all week.
You're on form today. Genuinely.
Whatever you're doing, keep doing it.
This is the good stuff.
I'm having a lovely time. Thought you should know.
Even the pigeons look cheerful today.
Days like this write themselves up nicely.
If you're keeping score, we're winning.

rules.note: A note after climbing out of a bad stretch. It used to trigger on a BOSS kill, which is the one kill that already has kill-boss-celebrate sitting on it at priority 70 - so whenever this matched, that matched too and outranked it, and this could only ever have fired in the celebration's cooldown gap. Two boss kills inside thirty seconds is not a thing, so it never fired at all. Ordinary kills now, where the big moment is not already spoken for, and above kill-cheer: the day turning is worth more than a generic cheer.
rules.about: After a kill, once its mood has climbed out of a bad stretch.
say: There. That's more like it.
See? The day turns.
That's the one we needed.
Better. Much better.
The day's looking up. Cautiously.
There it is. Knew it was in there somewhere.
Right, the slump's over. Onward.

rules.note: Notices the count. 'every': 25 fires on the twenty-fifth of THAT npc and every twenty-fifth after, with {count} carrying the number and {npc} the name. Nothing says paying attention like a tally.
rules.about: Every 25th kill of the same monster. {count} is the number and {npc} the name.
say: That's {count} of them. Not that I'm counting. I am counting.
{count}. I've been keeping track, since nobody else was.
{count}. The {npc} population is having a bad day.
Number {count}. You could stop. You won't, but you could.
{count}. At some point this stopped being a fight and became a job.
{count}. The tally marks are becoming a drawing.
{count}. The {npc} column's run off the page.
Entry {count}. Same as entry one, but later.

rules.note: The bigger milestone, at every hundredth of one npc. Higher priority than kill-tally so the round number wins when both come up together.
rules.about: Every 100th kill of the same monster.
say: {count}. I do hope this is all for something.
{count} of them. You realise that's a village?
{count}. I've watched every single one. Ask me anything.
That's {count}, and I'd like it noted that I never once complained.
{count}. Some scribes record wars smaller than this.
{count}. I had to start a second page.
{count}, and my quill would like a word.

rules.note: Notices the same animation running for about two minutes. Knows nothing about the skill - a repeating animation IS the activity, which covers every one of them at once, including ones added later.
rules.about: When you have been doing the same thing for about two minutes.
say: Still at it, then.
You've been doing that a while.
I've watched you do that about forty times now.
This is the part of the adventure the songs leave out.
Don't mind me. I'm just here.
We've been here a bit, haven't we.
Rhythm's good. I'd clap along, but no.
You've found your pace. Or it's found you.
That's the sound of industry, that is.
This is how ledgers get filled. Carry on.

rules.note: The same, much later - about eight minutes of one activity. Higher priority so it wins over the shorter one once it is due.
rules.about: When you have been doing the same thing for about eight minutes.
say: You've been doing this a very long time.
I stopped counting a while back. It was for my own good.
I want you to know I'm still here. Fading, but here.
At what point does this become a lifestyle?
I've had time to think. I have some concerns.
The birds have stopped commenting. Even they're used to it.
I've begun composing. It's an epic. It's about this.
I've noted your dedication. Repeatedly.
We may be here forever. There are worse spots.

rules.note: A few hours away. awayFor is the one thing the follower remembers between sessions, and it is what makes it feel like it existed while you were gone.
rules.about: Welcome back after a few hours away.
say: The notebook kept me company. It's not much of a talker.
Back, then. I did wonder.
Afternoon. Or evening. I've rather lost track.
You were gone a while. Everything's where you left it.
Hours, by my count. I don't get those wrong.
Back at last. I'd sharpened every quill I own.
Nothing happened. I wrote that down, too.

rules.note: The greeting that remembers what you were doing rather than how long it has been. lastTime is the last nameable thing the two of you did - the work, a boss, a level, a quest - carried across the logout. An hour away or more, and a chance roll so the plain away lines keep a share.
rules.about: A welcome back that remembers what you were last doing together, after an hour or more away. {lastTime} is that thing.
say: Back, then. Last time: {lastTime}.
Where were we? Ah, {lastTime}.
Last line in the book: {lastTime}.
You're back. Last entry: {lastTime}.

rules.note: The logout tab opened. The body turns and waves on its own (the moments, five minutes between waves); this is the rare word to go with it, and it must be short, because the click is coming.
rules.about: Now and then when you open the logout tab, a short word to go with its wave.
say: Off, then? I'll finish the page.
Go on. I'll be here.
Same time tomorrow, I expect.
Mind how you go.
I'll write up the rest myself.

rules.note: A drop of yours worth having that you walked away from. The follower has gone to stand by it; this is the one line. Only a thing that is still there and on screen, checked the tick it sets off.
rules.about: A drop worth having that you walked away from. It goes and stands by it. {thing} is the drop.
say: You've left your {thing} here.
The {thing}. It's still on the ground.
I'll stand by the {thing} until you notice it.
You're walking away from a {thing}.

rules.note: A bird's nest on the ground the player has not picked up.
rules.about: A bird's nest on the ground that you have not picked up.
say: A nest. Under the tree, where nests go.
There's a nest here. Might be something in it.
You've left a nest. I've noted where.

rules.note: An impling within sight. The follower steps toward it; it will not wait, and neither will the line.
rules.about: An impling within sight. The follower steps toward it. {thing} is the impling.
say: There's a {thing}. It won't wait.
{thing}, over here. For now, anyway.
A {thing}, if you're quick.
I see a {thing}. I'm not catching it for you.

rules.note: A crashed star, walked over to and written up. A date worth having.
rules.about: A crashed star, walked over to and written up.
say: A star. In the ground. I have the date and the place.
That fell out of the sky. It's getting a page of its own.
A crashed star. I've drawn it, badly.

rules.note: The player stopped beside a signpost, a statue, a plaque, and the scribe went to read it, notes out. The joke is the seriousness; the line stays dry.
rules.about: When you stop beside a signpost, statue or plaque, and it goes to read it.
say: It says something. I'm copying it out.
A {thing}. Somebody meant this to be read, so I'm reading it.
Hold on. I want the wording of this {thing} exactly.
Everything on this {thing} is in the book now.

rules.note: Sent across the ditch from the safe side. It has walked to the edge and turned to look at the player; it is not going over. Trico's beat of reluctance, with the honesty that it cannot cross anyway.
rules.about: When you send it across the Wilderness ditch. It stops at the edge and will not cross.
say: Not over that. I'll wait here.
The ditch is where my courage ends. I'll keep the notes safe this side.
You go on. Somebody has to live to write down what happened.
I'll watch from here. You get a good view of {thing} this side.

rules.note: Sent to a spot beside something twenty levels over the player. It stops three tiles short, looks back for a beat, and then goes. Not a refusal: the beat before yes.
rules.about: When you send it beside something twenty levels above you. It stops short, then goes.
say: Next to the {thing}? All right. Give me a moment.
I'm going. Not hurrying, with that {thing} there.
Right beside the {thing}. If you say so.
Let the {thing} see me and decide against it first.

rules.note: The player walked straight at the parked follower and it stepped aside at the last tick. Ellie's rule: not preemptively, and with a word about personal space, which is what made players respect her.
rules.about: When you walk straight at it while it stands still, it steps aside at the last moment.
say: Mind.
I was here first, you know.
Excuse me.
Go on, then. Don't mind me.
All this room and you pick my spot.

rules.note: A day or more. Higher priority so it wins over away-a-while.
rules.about: Welcome back after a day or more away.
say: Days, this time. I counted.
Ah, good. I was about to send out a search party. Of one.
That was a long one. Good to see you.
I was beginning to think you'd found a better follower.
Long enough that I kept checking the road.
Yesterday's page just says 'waited'. Today looks better.
You're back! I'd run out of things to underline.

rules.note: A week or more. The warmest of the three, and the highest priority.
rules.about: Welcome back after a week or more away.
say: You came back. I wasn't sure you would.
It's been weeks. Weeks! Where do I start.
Look who it is. Your page had gone a bit yellow.
I'd lost count of the days. Welcome back.
Weeks. I re-read the whole book waiting.
Long absence, short reunion speech: hello.
I'd started sketching. Don't ask to see them.

rules.note: Cooking gone wrong. The fragment 'accidentally burn' is confirmed against the live game - it fires. Leave it a fragment rather than the whole sentence: the food's name sits in the middle of it.
rules.about: When you burn food while cooking.
say: That was food, once.
I wasn't hungry anyway.
The fire wins again.
We'll call that a sacrifice.
That's carbon now. Historically, food.
The recipe said nothing about flames that tall.
Another one for the fire's collection.
Smells like progress. Burnt progress.

rules.note: An agility obstacle going badly. Confirm with ::follower chatwatch.
rules.about: When you slip on an agility obstacle.
say: Gravity's still undefeated, then.
I'd have caught you. Probably.
Nobody saw. Except everyone.
Up you get.
The ground moved. We'll say the ground moved.
Graceful. In a manner of speaking.
I'll leave that out of the notes. Kidding. It's in.

rules.note: Stamps its feet in the snow. Silent on purpose - a physical tell says more than a line about being cold. Animation 4278 is EMOTE_STAMPFEET, measured from the cache; the regions are ones RegionAudit has confirmed.
rules.about: Stamps its feet in the snow. No words.

rules.note: Said as the follower steps away. Everything until thieving-end is silent, and this is what makes that silence read as the follower keeping watch rather than as the follower having stopped working. Register is accomplice: we, lookout talk, and an alibi ready before anyone asks for one.
rules.about: When you start thieving: it steps away and keeps watch.
say: Go on. I've got the corner.
Eyes open. I'll whistle if anyone looks twice.
You work, I'll watch. Same as always.
I'll take the far side. Cough if it goes wrong.
Nobody's looking. Nobody who matters, anyway.
Right. I don't know you, you don't know me.
Take your time. I'm just admiring the architecture.
Say the word and we're both somewhere else entirely.
Left pocket. Trust me, it's always the left.
I count guards for a hobby. None at the moment.
Quick fingers, slow breathing. Off you go.
The trick is looking bored. I'm a natural.

rules.note: The other end, once the player has stopped or moved off. Same accomplice register as thieving-start - the job is over, the story is straight.
rules.about: When you stop thieving or move off.
say: Clean work. We were never here.
Nothing to see. Nothing at all.
That's the take, then. Walk normally.
Don't run. Running looks guilty.
We're done. Straighten your face.
Lovely. And if anyone asks, we were fishing.
Right, that's enough larceny for one afternoon.
Whatever that was, I was somewhere else at the time.
Pockets full, consciences clear enough.
A tidy bit of redistribution, that.
We'll split it later. By which I mean you keep it.
History will remember us kindly. It won't hear about this.

rules.note: Keeping watch while the player works. Animation 6840 is GENERIC_LOOK_AND_SEARCH, a look about that starts and ends standing, 3.4 ticks. The distant idle it replaced moved too little to read as anything. Silent by design - the whole session is muted, and an animation-only rule is movement rather than chatter so it plays anyway.
rules.about: Keeps watch while you steal. No words.
