rules.note: The 10th time the follower has been started up with this player. Pinned to the exact number with minimum and maximum, so the line can name it - 'every 25th' would have to stay vague. The count lives in the config and survives a logout, which is the whole point: a session counter that resets is not a memory.
rules.about: The 10th time you have played together.
say: Ten times now you've come back to me. I do notice, you know.
Ten. That's ten times we've set out together.

rules.note: The 50th time the follower has been started up with this player. Pinned to the exact number with minimum and maximum, so the line can name it - 'every 25th' would have to stay vague. The count lives in the config and survives a logout, which is the whole point: a session counter that resets is not a memory.
rules.about: The 50th time you have played together.
say: Fifty. Fifty times you've turned up. Not that I'm counting.
That's the fiftieth time you've brought me along. I kept count.

rules.note: The 100th time the follower has been started up with this player. Pinned to the exact number with minimum and maximum, so the line can name it - 'every 25th' would have to stay vague. The count lives in the config and survives a logout, which is the whole point: a session counter that resets is not a memory.
rules.about: The 100th time you have played together.
say: A hundred outings now. I'd go round again from the first.
One hundred. I don't know many who'd come back a hundred times.

rules.note: The 365th time the follower has been started up with this player. Pinned to the exact number with minimum and maximum, so the line can name it - 'every 25th' would have to stay vague. The count lives in the config and survives a logout, which is the whole point: a session counter that resets is not a memory.
rules.about: The 365th time you have played together.
say: Three hundred and sixty-five times out. One for every day of a year.
Three hundred and sixty-five outings. A page for every one.

rules.markHere: you hit harder than you ever had
rules.note: A new biggest hit. {value} is the new mark and {previous} the one it beat, which is what makes it land - a record without the old number is just a number. The first hit after an install seeds the record silently and says nothing, so this cannot fire on day one.
rules.about: Your biggest hit yet. {value} is the new best and {previous} the one it beat. Never on the first day.
say: {value}! Hardest I've ever seen you hit, and I was there for the {previous}.
{value} damage. You'd never got past {previous} before.
Did you see that? {value}. New best.
{value}. The old record was {previous}. Was.
A {value}! Underline it. Twice.
That's {value}, a new best. The book takes back what it said.

rules.note: The longest we have ever been out. Said once, on the minute it crosses - the plugin stores the mark every minute but only announces the crossing, or it would be a clock rather than a compliment.
rules.about: Your longest time out together yet, said the minute it is beaten. {value} is the minutes.
say: {value} minutes. That's the longest we've ever been out together.
We've been at this {value} minutes. Our best used to be {previous}.
This is officially the longest day we've had. {value} minutes.
{value} minutes and counting. A personal best, this.
That's {value} minutes out, a new record. The old one was {previous}.

rules.note: Dying when it is very much not the first time. The tally survives a logout, so 'again' means since we met rather than since you logged in - which is the difference between a companion and a scoreboard.
rules.about: Dying when it is very much not the first time: ten or more since you met.
say: Again? Right. Same page as last time, then.
You do this a lot, you know. I've been keeping track.
I've seen you die more times than I care to say.
This page is getting crowded.
There's a whole chapter on these now.
At this point I keep the quill out.
One more for a list I never wanted to start.
You and gravestones. A recurring theme.

rules.note: A level up when there have been a great many. Same lifetime tally.
rules.about: A level up when there have been a great many since you met.
say: Another one. You've had dozens since I've known you.
You keep doing that. I've watched you do it more often than anyone.
{skill} again. You never do stop, do you.
Another {skill} level. The column barely fits.
Up again. You collect these like feathers.
More {skill}. I'm running out of margin.
Most people would stop at this many levels. You show no sign of it.
That's another one written down. My wrist's starting to ache.

rules.note: The follower answering YOU rather than the world. from:player and is:PUBLICCHAT together are what stop it greeting the whole street - the chat type name is exactly what ::follower chatwatch prints.
rules.about: When you say hi, hey or hello in public chat.
say: Hello to you too.
Oh, hello. Was that for me?
Hello! Right, I'm listening.
Hey yourself.
Present and accounted for.
Afternoon. Or whatever it is.
Yes, hello. Still here.
At your service. Within reason.

rules.note: Laughing because you did. Not because anything was funny.
rules.about: Laughing because you did in public chat. Not because anything was funny.
say: I don't know what's funny but I'm in.
Ha! Yes. Whatever that was.
Look at us, having a laugh.
That's the spirit.
Comedy. I'm noting the date.
Heh. All right, that got me.
If you're laughing, I'm laughing.

rules.note: Being thanked. Rarely happens; worth having a line ready.
rules.about: When you say thanks in public chat.
say: Any time. Genuinely.
Don't mention it. Please do mention it again though.
That's what I'm here for.
You're welcome. I'll be smug about it all day.
Careful. I'll come to expect gratitude.
I'll file that under rare events.
Well now, manners. How lovely.

rules.note: Being LOOKED at. The mouse resting on the follower for eight ticks is attention; a cursor crossing the screen is not, which is what the tick count is for. Costs nothing to know - the clickbox is already projected every client tick to draw the hover hint.
rules.about: When your mouse rests on it for a few seconds.
say: Yes? Something on my face?
I can see you looking.
Hello. You've been staring a while.
Go on then, get a good look.
Still here. Still fascinating, apparently.
Take notes if you like. I do.
I'd pose, but this is my only expression.

rules.note: Being looked up. The game gives its line about the follower; this is the follower's line about being looked up.
rules.about: When you examine it.
say: Yes, that's me. All of that is true.
Reading up on me, are you?
Always writing something. They're not wrong.
Accurate, if a bit brief.
Somebody wrote that about me. Fair play.
That's the official version. The real one's longer.
Examined! I feel positively catalogued.
Go on, read the whole entry. I'll wait.
That description undersells the notebook.
Careful. I examine back.

rules.note: A question, which is a different thing from a remark. asks names a tree in dialogs.json; while the question is open, right-clicking Talk-to opens THAT conversation instead of the everyday one, and picking a branch is the answer. It used to want a word typed into public chat, which asked the player to know a magic word and asked the follower to listen to the whole street. The window is opened by SAYING it, so a question the mute swallowed leaves nothing waiting.
rules.about: Asks you a question. Talk to it to answer.
say: There's something I want to ask you. Talk to me when you have a moment.
Come and talk to me a minute? It's nothing bad.
When you get a second, talk to me. I've got a question.
I'd like a word, when you're not busy.
A word, when your hands are free.
No hurry, but come and find me for a minute.
Something to ask. Talk to me when you're ready.
Next time there's a lull, come and find me. I've got a small proposal.

rules.note: The follower asking for something, which is the only thing in the whole rule set that runs the other way round: everything else is a reaction to what you did, and this makes the next few minutes an answer to what IT said. Going to region 12850 within twenty minutes fulfils it; the deadline passing expires it. Three of these at descending priority with a chance roll, so the place asked for varies - only one want can be open at a time.
rules.about: Asks to go to Lumbridge. Take it there within twenty minutes and it is pleased.
say: Can we go back to Lumbridge? Everyone starts there.
Lumbridge, then. I want to check something in my notes.
Lumbridge next? The early pages need checking.
I'd like to see Lumbridge again. Old ground makes good notes.

rules.note: The follower asking for something, which is the only thing in the whole rule set that runs the other way round: everything else is a reaction to what you did, and this makes the next few minutes an answer to what IT said. Going to region 12598 within twenty minutes fulfils it; the deadline passing expires it. Three of these at descending priority with a chance roll, so the place asked for varies - only one want can be open at a time.
rules.about: Asks to go to the Grand Exchange. Take it there within twenty minutes and it is pleased.
say: The Grand Exchange, please. Prices change and mine are out of date.
Take me to the Exchange? I want to hear what things cost.
The Exchange, when you can. My price list is a relic.
Take me past the Exchange. I miss the shouting.

rules.note: The follower asking for something, which is the only thing in the whole rule set that runs the other way round: everything else is a reaction to what you did, and this makes the next few minutes an answer to what IT said. Going to region 10293 within twenty minutes fulfils it; the deadline passing expires it. Three of these at descending priority with a chance roll, so the place asked for varies - only one want can be open at a time.
rules.about: Asks to go to the Fishing Guild. Take it there within twenty minutes and it is pleased.
say: Then the Fishing Guild. Nothing to record there. That's rather the point.
The Fishing Guild, if you're offering. I'd like to see the water.
The Fishing Guild would do nicely. Water and no surprises.
Somewhere quiet next. The Fishing Guild does quiet properly.

rules.note: Turned down. Gracious about it, because sulking would only teach the player not to answer.
rules.about: When you say no to a question it asked.
say: Fair enough. Another time.
No bother. Forget I asked.
Right you are. Carry on.
Say no more. Consider it withdrawn.
Not the answer I'd hoped for, but an answer.
Point taken. No hard feelings.

rules.note: The player actually went. This is the payoff for the whole want mechanism and the biggest single mood swing in the file: a thing with desires that can be SATISFIED reads as alive in a way no amount of commentary manages. {want} names the place it asked for.
rules.about: When you take it where it asked to go. {want} is the place.
say: {want}! You actually brought me. Thank you.
You remembered. We're in {want}. I'm delighted.
Look at that - {want}. You didn't have to do that.
{want}, like I asked. You're all right, you are.
{want}, as requested. You take requests.
We made it to {want}. The notes thank you.
And here we are. {want}. Good as your word.

rules.note: Asked for, never done. A small drop, not a sulk - it has to be survivable or the follower becomes a chore.
rules.about: When it asked to go somewhere and you never went. {want} is the place.
say: We never did get to {want}. Never mind.
I'd given up on {want} anyway.
So much for {want}, then.
The page for {want} stays half written.
{want} will keep. Everything keeps.
Maybe {want} next time, then.

rules.note: Somewhere THIS follower is fond of. The set is rolled once per character from the regions the rule set already has opinions about, then kept for good - so two people do not get the same follower, and the mood stops being weather and becomes a temperament you can learn.
rules.about: Somewhere this follower is fond of. Each follower has its own favourites, picked once and kept.
say: I do like it here. I don't know why. I just do.
This is one of my places, this.
Oh, good. I like this one.
We should come here more.
This place agrees with me. I feel better already.
Good air here. Good everything, really.
Add this one to the short list.

rules.note: The other half of the same coin. A follower with no dislikes has no taste, only enthusiasm.
rules.about: Somewhere this follower dislikes. Each follower has its own, picked once and kept.
say: Here again. I've never liked this place.
Something about this spot puts me off. Always has.
Can we not stay here long?
I'd rather be almost anywhere else, if I'm honest.
This place and I have an understanding. We don't get on.
The notes on this spot are all in a darker ink.
Every visit here feels a page too long.
We're back HERE. Wonderful. I'll keep my coat on.
This place again. My handwriting gets worse just standing in it.

rules.note: A WARNING rather than a report. Two slots left, not none: reacting before is the thing that reads as a mind paying attention, and reacting after is only narration. Counted by walking the container, so it is right whichever way round size() and count() are. In the gear group, which the settings call Items: that is where a player looks for it.
rules.about: A warning when your bag has two slots left.
say: You're nearly out of room, you know.
Two slots left. Just so you've heard it from someone.
Bag's about full. Might want to do something about that.
Bag check: nearly full. That's the whole report.
You're down to your last two slots.
The bag's not getting any emptier.
Almost out of room. I want it on the record that I said so.
It's getting a bit tight in there.
Whatever you pick up next had better be worth a slot.
The bag and I agree: something has to go.
Nearly full. I'll stop mentioning it eventually.
How attached are you to everything in there?
Everything in there was essential at the time.
You're two items from a difficult decision.
That bag has ambitions above its size.
Consider this the polite warning. The bag won't give one.
I'm keeping a list of what you won't part with.
The bank, then? I'll allow it this once.
There's space for two more mistakes.
Something in there will have to become a memory.
The bag's at the stage where I'd start choosing.
The ground is always an option. A poor one.
I'd hate for the next good thing to have nowhere to go.
Shall I pretend I didn't see the bag?

rules.note: Nerves. npcNearby with a combat level and no names at all, so this covers every large thing in the game and everything added later without a list to maintain. Suppressed during a fight - once it has started, saying something big is nearby is not news.
rules.about: Nerves, when something very large is close by. Not during a fight.
say: That thing is very large and very close.
You have seen what's standing over there? Just checking.
We're stood very close to something that could end this quickly.
Are we meant to be this close to that?
Official measurement: enormous.
I'm noting its size from a distance. There is no safe distance.

rules.note: Crowd awareness. Six people inside six tiles is a bank, an event, or a queue - all of them worth a word.
rules.about: Now and then when six or more people are within six tiles.
say: Busy here, isn't it.
Everyone's turned up at once.
I can't move for people.
Is something happening, or is it always like this?
Half the world's here and the other half's queuing.
A crowd. My notes prefer them at a distance.
Mind your pockets. I'm minding mine.
All these people, and not one of them taking notes.

rules.note: A flinch, and nothing else. Animation 424 is HUMAN_UNARMEDBLOCK, 1.26s, the unarmed defensive recoil. Silent on purpose: a body that reacts before the mouth does is most of what makes something look like it is watching, and a line here would be one more thing said during a fight that is already noisy.
rules.about: Flinches when you take a big hit. No words.

rules.note: Arriving where it asked, with the REASON. The generic line thanks you for coming; this says why that place and not another, which is the difference between a companion that is pleased and one that has a preference. Above the generic want-fulfilled at 78, which stays as the fallback for any want without a line of its own. hushMs takes the floor for 10 seconds: the region change raises an area line at the same instant, and two lines about one arrival is one too many.
rules.about: When you take it to Lumbridge as it asked, it says why it wanted to go.
say: Lumbridge. Everyone's first steps happen here. Mine were with you.
Look at the church. Over two hundred years old, and still standing.
Castle, river, old stone. Nothing happens here. That's the appeal.
Thank you. Nobody's in a hurry in Lumbridge. Look at it.

rules.note: Arriving where it asked, with the REASON. The generic line thanks you for coming; this says why that place and not another, which is the difference between a companion that is pleased and one that has a preference. Above the generic want-fulfilled at 78, which stays as the fallback for any want without a line of its own. hushMs takes the floor for 10 seconds: the region change raises an area line at the same instant, and two lines about one arrival is one too many.
rules.about: When you take it to the Grand Exchange as it asked, it says why it wanted to go.
say: Everyone at the Exchange wants something. You can see it on them.
Listen to it. Hundreds of people haggling at once. I could watch all day.
It's the noise I like. Nowhere else in the world sounds like this.
Fortunes made and lost before lunch, and I get to watch.

rules.note: Arriving where it asked, with the REASON. The generic line thanks you for coming; this says why that place and not another, which is the difference between a companion that is pleased and one that has a preference. Above the generic want-fulfilled at 78, which stays as the fallback for any want without a line of its own. hushMs takes the floor for 10 seconds: the region change raises an area line at the same instant, and two lines about one arrival is one too many.
rules.about: When you take it to the Fishing Guild as it asked, it says why it wanted to go.
say: The Fishing Guild. It's the quiet. You don't get quiet like this anywhere.
Listen. Nothing. Just the water. I needed this.
Nothing here is trying to kill us. Do you know how rare that is?
The water does something to me. Sorry. I know it's only water.

rules.note: Filed when you come out the far side of nearly dying. The follower does not need to say anything at the time - critical-hp already does - it just needs to remember, so it can bring it up later. The particulars (who, which item, where, when) are filled in when it is filed, so a recall can jog the memory rather than allude to it.
rules.about: Remembers when you nearly die, to bring up later.

remember.as: how close that was with the {foe}

rules.note: The obvious one. Filed on every death, so the count is what makes the recall land: once is bad luck, four times is a habit. The particulars (who, which item, where, when) are filled in when it is filed, so a recall can jog the memory rather than allude to it.
rules.about: Remembers when you die, to bring up later.

remember.as: the way that went with the {foe}

say: That's going in the book.
I saw all of it, for what it's worth.
The record will be kind about it.
I've written it down. Not happily.
Some entries I would rather not have.
Filed under things we don't mention.
The ink went on heavier than usual for that one.
I wrote it smaller, so it looks further away.
One more for the chapter I keep meaning to close.

rules.note: Filed on a drop big enough to still be talking about an hour later. Above the loot-celebrate threshold so the celebration wins the event and this one only files - two lines about one drop is one too many, and the recall is the part that matters here. The particulars (who, which item, where, when) are filled in when it is filed, so a recall can jog the memory rather than allude to it.
rules.about: Remembers a really big drop, to bring up later.
say: I'm still not over that.
That drop gets its own footnote.
I re-read that entry sometimes. For morale.
Best line in the ledger so far.

rules.note: Filed when something with a combat level in three figures stops moving. Low priority so the celebration rules win the kill. The particulars (who, which item, where, when) are filled in when it is filed, so a recall can jog the memory rather than allude to it.
rules.about: Remembers a kill of something level 150 or higher, to bring up later.
say: I want that written down somewhere.
That one goes in with a steadier hand.
Chapters end on moments like that.
Tell people. If you don't, I will.

rules.note: The whole point of the incident. Brought up unprompted, in a quiet moment, about the specific thing that happened rather than about the number of times something like it has. Deliberately rare.
rules.about: In a quiet moment, it brings up something it remembers. {memory} is that thing.
say: I keep thinking about {memory}.
I was rereading the entry on {memory}.
Do you ever think about {memory}? I do.
It's quiet. My mind goes back to {memory}.

rules.note: The third death exactly, so the count is true when it is said. The death being spoken of is filed after the line is chosen, so the count read here is the deaths before it: two. Outranks recall-death-again, which takes over from the fourth.
rules.about: Your third death that it remembers.
say: That's three. I've started keeping count, and I wish I hadn't.

rules.note: Named rather than generic, because the count is the joke and only this incident has a count worth making one of. The count read is the deaths before this one, so a minimum of 2 is the third death on.
rules.about: Every death after the third that it remembers.
say: I'm starting to see a pattern, and I don't like it.
We've done this before. Several times. Recently.
Same ending, new page.
The entries are starting to rhyme.
I'd say lightning doesn't strike twice, but here we are.
At this point the margin notes are just sighs.
I could trace this one straight off the last.

rules.note: The line that could not exist without incidents: advice with a reason attached, and the reason is something you were both there for. Fires on going back into a fight, not on idling.
rules.about: Sometimes, as a fight starts, a warning about a close call it remembers. {memory} is that.
say: Careful. I've not forgotten {memory}.
Before you start. Remember {memory}?
Go on then. But I'm watching, after {memory}.
Mind how you go. The ink's barely dry on {memory}.
Off you go. My mind's still half on {memory}.

rules.note: Back in the region the incident happened in. The rule is state, so it fires once on the rising edge, which is the moment of arriving; the cooldown keeps a day at the same spot to one remark.
rules.about: Back in the place where the thing it keeps bringing up happened. {memory} is that thing.
say: The notes on {memory} start here.
Here again, and I've not forgotten {memory}.
This is where I wrote down {memory}.
The page on {memory} is still creased.

rules.note: One of the things the incident was with, back in sight. {memoryWho} is the NPC's name off the record; memoryFoeNearby guarantees it is there to print.
rules.about: When a creature from the thing it keeps bringing up is in sight. {memoryWho} is its name and {memory} the thing.
say: That's a {memoryWho}. You'll remember {memory}.
A {memoryWho}. I remember {memory}.
Mind the {memoryWho}. My page on it isn't a kind one.
There's the {memoryWho}. I was there for {memory}.
A {memoryWho}. That shape's on a page I keep going back to.

rules.note: Picks something up and carries it about for a while. It only counts if it was SAID - a souvenir nobody was told about is invisible - and it refuses while already carrying something, or the follower silently swaps out an object it has been talking about.
rules.about: Picks up a rock and carries it about for a while.
say: Hold on. Look at this rock. Perfectly flat.
I'm taking this rock. It's a good rock and I'll hear nothing else.
One more rock for the collection. The collection is one rock.
Flat, grey, dependable. This rock has everything.

rules.note: Picks something up and carries it about for a while. It only counts if it was SAID - a souvenir nobody was told about is invisible - and it refuses while already carrying something, or the follower silently swaps out an object it has been talking about.
rules.about: Picks up a stick and carries it about for a while.
say: Wait. This stick's interesting. I couldn't tell you why.
I'm keeping this stick. Don't look at me like that.
A stick with character. You don't see many.
This stick has a future. I can't say what kind.

rules.note: Picks something up and carries it about for a while. It only counts if it was SAID - a souvenir nobody was told about is invisible - and it refuses while already carrying something, or the follower silently swaps out an object it has been talking about.
rules.about: Picks up a pebble and carries it about for a while.
say: That pebble's lucky. I can tell. Give me a second.
Finders keepers. This pebble's coming with me.
Look how smooth this is. I'm having it.
A pebble like this doesn't come along twice.

rules.note: Picks something up and carries it about for a while. It only counts if it was SAID - a souvenir nobody was told about is invisible - and it refuses while already carrying something, or the follower silently swaps out an object it has been talking about.
rules.about: Picks up a feather and carries it about for a while.
say: A feather. Right. In the pocket it goes.
Somebody dropped a feather here. Their loss.
A feather in decent condition. The day's looking up.
This feather's too good to leave lying about. I'll take it.

rules.note: Picks something up and carries it about for a while. It only counts if it was SAID - a souvenir nobody was told about is invisible - and it refuses while already carrying something, or the follower silently swaps out an object it has been talking about.
rules.about: Picks up a bent nail and carries it about for a while.
say: Look, a nail. Bent, but still a nail.
A bent nail. That'll come in useful one day.
One bent nail, slightly historic. Mine now.
You'd be amazed what a nail can fix. Not this one. Still.
I could do with a feather, if one turns up.
Quills wear out. Keep an eye open for a feather.
If a bird's been careless anywhere near you, I'd take the feather.
A feather would do. The old quill's more stump than quill.
Not to nag, but a feather wouldn't go amiss. For the writing.
Papyrus, if you pass any. Mine's nearly out.
Running low on papyrus. The good pages go fast.
The margins are doing overtime. Papyrus, if you see any.
If you see papyrus, think of me. Then pick it up.
I write small, but not that small. Papyrus, please.
A ball of wool would tie these scrolls properly.
The scrolls keep unrolling. A ball of wool would fix that.
Wool, if you spot some. My scrolls are currently a loose confederation.
Not urgent, but a ball of wool would bring some order to the satchel.
A ball of wool, before this bundle flaps itself to bits.
Soft clay, if you see any. Seals want stamping.
I could use soft clay. Official documents deserve a seal.
Some soft clay would help. Don't ask what for. It's a surprise.
If any soft clay comes your way, I've got plans for it. Small plans.
I'm making something and it's going badly. Soft clay would save it.
Charcoal, if any crosses your path. For the rough sketches.
A bit of charcoal would be welcome. Some things get drawn, not written.
If charcoal turns up, I'll take it. The sketches are getting faint.
Somebody has to draw the crates. I'll need charcoal for that.
A stick of charcoal would do. I've been sketching with a burnt twig.

rules.note: The player picked 'Found you that <wish>.' AND the thing is really in their bag - checked, because play testing produced the bluff within minutes. Nothing is consumed (client-side), but presence is honest.
rules.about: When you hand over the thing it wished for and it really is in your bag. {wish} is the thing.
say: That {wish}. Exactly what I needed.
The {wish}! You remembered. I won't forget that.
Perfect. The {wish} goes in the good pocket.
You actually found the {wish}. The ledger tips your way.
My old {wish} for your new one. Even, which is how I like it.
Take my worn {wish} in exchange. It's got years left in it.
A trade rather than a gift. You keep my old {wish}, I keep yours.
The {wish} is mine now and my old one's yours. Nobody's poorer.
Here, have my tired old {wish}. It's still good for something.
A fresh {wish}. You'll hardly notice, but I very much will.
I took the fresh {wish} and left you my old one. Only manners.
You've still got my old {wish}. I don't leave you short.
The old {wish} is yours. Don't look at it too closely.
Thank you. My worn {wish} is yours, if you want it.

rules.note: The wish granted while the pocket already holds a souvenir: the follower trades up, out loud. A gift outranks a rock it found itself, and a SPOKEN swap is honest where a silent one was the thing the old deferral rule existed to prevent. Deferring instead parked the option for the length of a ninety-minute carry, which play testing read as the option refusing to go away.
rules.about: When you hand over its wish while it already carries something, and it swaps them. {souvenir} is what it puts down.
say: The {wish}! I'll set down {souvenir} to make room.
A trade, then: {souvenir} out, the {wish} in.
The {wish} outranks {souvenir}. Out it goes.
Trading {souvenir} for the {wish}. Back to you.
The {wish} bumps {souvenir}. Have my old one.

rules.note: The empty-bag claim, already caught IN the dialog box - the script branches on the bag, because a neutral box read as the follower not looking. This is the dry coda afterwards, not a second telling-off, so it needs no {wish} and no bag re-check.
rules.about: After you claimed to have its wish with nothing in your bag.
say: That's going on your record, you know.
Filed under: nice try.

rules.note: The mid-box race: the bag had the thing when the box opened and not when the branch was picked. The box already said 'that is the one', so silence here would read as the follower being fooled - and this follower checks.
rules.about: When you offer its wish but it has left your bag before you finish. {wish} is the thing.
say: Where did the {wish} go? It was in there a moment ago.
You had it just now. I watched the bag. Bring it back.

rules.note: The race: the wish lapsed between the box opening and the click. Rare, but silence there reads as a bug.
rules.about: When you offer its wish just after it has stopped wishing for it.
say: Kind of you. The moment's rather passed, but kind of you.
I'd stopped hoping for that one. Appreciated all the same.

rules.note: Brings up the thing it is holding. This is the payoff for the object existing at all: it is the same rock forty minutes later.
rules.about: Brings up the thing it is holding. {souvenir} is the thing.
say: I've still got {souvenir}, in case you were wondering.
Still carrying {souvenir}. No regrets.
I've got {souvenir}. You've not asked about it once.
I'm looking after {souvenir}. It's safe and well.
Me and {souvenir}, still going strong.
I've carried {souvenir} through some things today.
I've grown attached to {souvenir}. Don't tell anyone.
I'm keeping {souvenir}. Not up for discussion.

rules.note: And one day it is not the same rock. The name survives the loss so the line can mourn it properly.
rules.about: When it loses the thing it was carrying. {souvenir} is the thing.
say: I've lost {souvenir}. Somewhere back there.
I've lost {souvenir}. I'd rather not talk about it.
Right, well. That's {souvenir} gone, then.
A moment of silence for {souvenir}.
We're down {souvenir}. Somewhere muddy, probably.
Gone. I didn't do right by {souvenir}.

rules.note: The optimist. Same machinery, other direction, so being wrong is on the table for both of them.
rules.about: Sometimes, as a fight starts, it bets something valuable will drop within five minutes.
say: I've got a feeling about this one. A good feeling.
This is the one. Don't ask me how I know.
Mark this fight. Something's coming off it.
Next drop's a good one. Put it in writing. I just did.
Call it instinct. This one pays.
Today's the day the luck pays out. You heard it here first.
I've done the arithmetic on this one. It's owed.
Watch this next bit. I've gone on record.

rules.note: Above the loot rules so the verdict on the prediction beats the remark about the prize. The follower called it; that is the story.
rules.about: When its bet on a fight comes true.
say: Told you.
I said. I did say.
And that's why you listen to me.
Called it. Not a word of thanks, mind.
As predicted. The book never lies.
Right again. Try to look surprised.

rules.note: The half that makes the other half worth anything.
rules.about: When its bet on a fight does not come true.
say: I was wrong. Enjoy it, it doesn't happen often.
Well. Ignore everything I said.
That's not what I predicted. Moving on.
We'll not speak of this again.
The prediction business is harder than it looks.
Strike that entry. Carefully, so nobody can read it.

rules.note: minimum and maximum are hours, and the comparison wraps past midnight, so this window is written the way a person says it.
rules.about: Now and then between 1 and 4 in the morning, by your own clock.
say: You do know what time it is.
It's the small hours. I'm not judging. I'm noticing.
Everyone sensible's asleep. I'm nearly one of them.
The birds'll start up soon. Just so you know.
The candle's low. Metaphorically. Go to bed.
Night watchmen keep better hours than this.
The moon and I think you should stop soon.

rules.note: The two facts together, which is a different remark from either of them alone: it is late AND we have been at this for hours.
rules.about: Late at night, after three hours or more of play.
say: Whatever this is, it'll still be here tomorrow.
This late, and this long at it. Go to bed. I'll keep watch.
I'm not going to stop you. I am going to keep mentioning it.
Long day, late hour. The maths says rest.
Even the ink wants to sleep.
Tomorrow exists. I've seen the schedule.

rules.note: Early, which is either admirable or the other thing.
rules.about: Now and then between 5 and 7 in the morning, by your own clock.
say: Up early, or not been to bed? I won't ask.
This is a respectable hour to be out. Barely.
Morning. Whichever side of it you're on.
Morning light. Good for reading, better for walking.
The day's fresh. Let's not waste it standing about.
Dawn patrol, is it? I'm awake. Mostly.

rules.note: Pinned with a maximum so the two-hour line does not keep being true at four hours and shout over the four-hour one.
rules.about: Now and then two hours into a session.
say: Two hours. I checked. Twice.
We've been at this two hours. I've enjoyed most of it.
Two hours in. The entry just says 'continued'.
That's two hours. My feet filed the first complaint.
Past the two-hour mark. You're nothing if not consistent.

rules.note: Five hours. Said once, and meant.
rules.about: Five hours into a session. Said once, and meant.
say: Five hours. Stand up, walk about. I'll still be here.
That's most of a day, that is. Have you eaten?
Five hours together. I've seen marriages with less.
A full day's work and then some. My quill's gone soft.
The sun's done most of an arc and neither of us noticed.
Whole chapters have passed. Stretch, at least.

rules.note: Three outings taken. The follower is not thanking you for the last one; it is thanking you for the pattern, which is the difference between politeness and knowing somebody.
rules.about: Now and then, once you have taken it on three of its outings.
say: You've humoured my outings. I've filed that somewhere safe.
I ask for an outing and off we go. Not everyone would.
No complaints. That's not something I say lightly.
For the record, you keep your promises.
Everywhere I ask to go, we go. Don't think I haven't noticed.
Your side of the favours ledger is looking healthy.

rules.note: And the other ledger. Not sulking - noting. A follower that forgot the times you said no would not be much of a companion either.
rules.about: Now and then, once you have skipped three of its outings and taken none.
say: That's a few times I've asked to go somewhere. I'm not sulking.
I ask less than I used to. You may have noticed.
Next time I ask, I'll set my hopes low first.
The requests column has a lot of blank replies.
I mention places. We stay put. It's a pattern.
Fine. The wanting was probably good for me.

rules.note: Held as a POSE, because these all loop: mining 624-629/642/3873/4482 (frameStep 8), woodcutting 867-879/2117/2846/5383 (frameStep 6), fishing 618-623 (frameStep 42/44/2) and fletching 1248 (frameStep 15), all measured. The pose is released when your animation changes, which is what joining in until you stop actually means. atTheWork has it walk over first and copy from a tile the game would let you work from, facing the middle of the tree or rock, and stop the moment it is moved off it.
rules.about: Joins in when you mine, cut trees, fish or fletch, until you stop.

rules.note: The same idea for the animations the cache says are ONE-SHOTS (frameStep -1): cooking 896/897, smithing 898/6712, crafting 1249. The server restarts these every cycle, so the follower having a single go and stopping is right; held as a pose they would loop wrong. atTheWork makes the go from beside the range or anvil, facing it, and then back to its seat. 4969 and 4975 used to be listed here as herblore and firemaking; they are the skill-cape emotes, not work.
rules.about: Has a go when you cook, smith or craft.

rules.note: Said occasionally instead of silently copying you, so the joining in reads as deliberate rather than as a rendering bug. Priority above the two mimes so it takes the tick when it wins.
rules.about: Now and then, instead of copying you quietly, it owns up.
say: I've been copying you a while now. You've not noticed.
I'm joining in. You carry on.
It looked easy when you were doing it.
I could do this. Given the tools. And the levels.
Yes, I'm copying you. No, I won't be stopping.
In my defence, it looked fun. It was fun.
Purely observational. Ignore the arms.
My hands are empty, but the technique's all there.
Don't stare. I lose my place.
Is this how you hold it? I've been guessing.
I'll stop when you stop. It seemed only fair.
Not copying. Corroborating.
One of us is producing something. It isn't me.
I'd log the hours, but there's no column for it.
The notes can wait. This is research.
You keep the pace. I'll keep the form.

rules.note: Buries along with you. 827 is HUMAN_PICKUPFLOOR, the bend the bury uses, proven on the follower by the bootlace and cat errands. A one-shot, so mirrored as an emote; the chance keeps it from copying every bone in the pile.
rules.about: Sometimes buries bones along with you.

rules.note: Casts along with you, rarely. The utility spells only: low and high alchemy 712/713, the three enchants 719-721, superheat 725 and charge orb 726, all HUMAN_CAST one-shots from the cache. The graphic copies through the mirror's twelve-tick window. Five percent with a minute between, so it reads as joining in once, not as a second caster.
rules.about: Now and then casts along with you: alchemy, enchanting, superheat and charging orbs.

rules.note: A shake of the head at a run of burnt food. The game says "You accidentally burn the shrimps." and every third of those, while a cooking session is on, earns 856 (EMOTE_NO, proven by the answered-no rule). Silent: the head says it. The working condition comes first so the count only runs during the session.
rules.about: Shakes its head at every third burnt food while you cook.

rules.note: Counts your batches: every fifth fletching animation earns a nod, 855 (EMOTE_YES, in the mirrored emotes). 1248 is HUMAN_FLETCHING, the one the mime-loops rule already holds; the server restarts it per bow, and each restart is one animation event. Only while the fletching session is on.
rules.about: Nods at every fifth item you fletch.

rules.note: Guarded with none/asking so it cannot replace a question already waiting for an answer. Without that, offering a game silently withdraws the outing and the player answers a question nothing is listening for.
rules.about: Offers you a game. Talk to it to play.
say: I've thought of a game. Come and talk to me.
Talk to me a minute. I want to try something.
I'm bored. Come here, I've had an idea.
Got a minute? Pick a hand. Come and see.
A quick game, if you're willing. Come talk to me.
Fancy a game? You know where I am.

rules.note: Half of the coin flip. This one is gated on chance 50 and sits above the losing rule, so a failed roll falls through to it: one winner per event by priority is what makes that a fair fifty-fifty rather than two rules both firing.
rules.about: The guessing game: you picked the right hand.
say: It was. How did you do that?
Right first time. I'm slightly annoyed.
There it is. You're better at this than me.
Correct. I had it there the whole time.
Yes. Annoyingly, yes.
You read me like a page.
That's the one. I need better hands.

rules.note: The other half. No chance gate: it fires whenever the winning rule did not, which is exactly half the time.
rules.about: The guessing game: you picked the wrong hand.
say: Wrong hand. It was the other one.
No. Other one. Bad luck.
Nothing in that one. Try again sometime.
Wrong. I won't gloat. I'm gloating.
Empty. The other one, always the other one.
Not that hand. This delights me.
Missed. My secrets survive another day.

rules.note: So that saying no is answered rather than ignored.
rules.about: The guessing game: you said no to playing.
say: Suit yourself. One of them's still full.
Your loss. Probably.
Some other time, then.
Fair. It wasn't much of a prize.
No? I'll play against myself, then. I usually win.

rules.note: A score is a running total of what the rules said moments here were worth, so this only reaches -80 after several bad ones. Priority above place-disliked, which would otherwise win with a milder line.
rules.about: A place where enough has gone wrong that it has come to hate it.
say: I hate it here, and I've got reasons. You were there for all of them.
Nothing good has ever happened to us in this place. Nothing.
Every time we come here, all I think about is leaving.
The evidence against this place keeps arriving.
This spot owes us. It knows what it did.
The file on this place is thick, and none of it flattering.
Here we are again, where most of our bad luck happens.
I've counted what this place has cost us. Twice, to be sure.

rules.note: The player picked 'You all right?' on a lowish day. Asking is the kindness; this is the lift and one soft overhead coda after the box closes.
rules.about: When you ask 'You all right?' on one of its lower days.
say: I'm lighter for being asked, oddly enough.
You checked on me. That does help.

rules.note: The roll says it hates this place; the earned score says good things keep happening here. feelsAbout already answers 'liked' - the override won - so this is the follower conceding the evidence while keeping the grudge, which is the only moment the temperament is visible as a temperament.
rules.about: A place it dislikes, though good things keep happening there.
say: I know. Good things happen here. I still don't like it.
The ledger likes this place. The ledger doesn't have to stand in it.
Fine, it's been lucky for us. Lucky and unlovely.

rules.note: The mirror: rolled fondness against earned bad luck. Loyalty, argued with the record.
rules.about: A place it likes, though bad luck keeps happening there.
say: Nothing but trouble for us here, I know. I like it anyway. Don't ask.
The record is against this place. I'm not. Loyalty is like that.

rules.note: The other end of the same total.
rules.about: A place where enough has gone right that it has come to like it.
say: Good things happen here. I've kept count, and they do.
I like this place, and for once I can tell you exactly why.
We've had some luck here. Long may it continue.
This place's tally is well in the black.
This spot's earned its good name with me, fair and square.

rules.note: What the place itself holds, via markHere on the rules that won those moments. Waits for you to come back to it, which is the whole difference from the incident: that one follows you about.
rules.about: Back somewhere something memorable happened. {here} is what happened.
say: This is where {here}. I remember it.
Same spot. This is where {here}.
Stand here a second. This is where {here}.
You may not remember. This is where {here}.
I've got this spot marked. It's where {here}.
Here. Right here. This is where {here}.

rules.note: The other half of a warning. Until now the follower shouted and then never mentioned it again, whichever way it went, which is the difference between commentary and a conversation.
rules.about: When you follow a warning it gave you.
say: Thank you. That's all I wanted.
There. Was that so hard?
Good. I'll stop going on about it.
You listened. I'm putting that in the book.
You actually took my advice. Banner day, this.
See? Painless.
And that's why I bother saying things.
Good. The book gets a tidy little tick.
Sensible. I'll not let it go to your head.
We work well when you do as I say. Coincidence, I'm sure.
Ah. So you do hear me.
Was that on my account, or were you going to anyway?
Quietly pleased. That's as loud as I get.
Right on cue. I'll pretend I timed that.
I'll take that as listening. Don't correct me.
Underlined. It's my page, I'll underline what I like.
There's a version of this where I had to ask twice.
My reputation as an oracle survives another day.
Did that help? I'll write it down as though it did.
Nothing left to nag about. I'll find something.

rules.note: And the funnier half.
rules.about: When you ignore a warning it gave you.
say: Right. I'll stop saying it, then.
I did mention it. For the record.
No? Fine. It's your skin.
I'll just say it to myself next time.
Ignoring me is a decision too. I've written it down.
The margin note here just says 'told them'.
As you like. The page remembers.
One day the ledger of ignored advice gets read aloud.
Duly noted. Duly ignored. The usual.

rules.note: The ledger, the same shape as the outings one: ten pieces of advice into the wind is a fact about the pair of you rather than about any one of them.
rules.about: Now and then, once you have ignored ten or more of its warnings.
say: At least ten times I've told you something, and you did as you liked.
Stopped counting how often you ignore me. That's a lie. I know exactly.
You never listen. I've decided that's part of your charm.
My advice does its best work as background noise.
I run an advice column for one reader, and you skip it.
One day you'll take a suggestion and I'll faint.

rules.note: And the warm end of it.
rules.about: Now and then, once you have followed ten or more of its warnings.
say: You actually listen to me. Do you know how rare that is?
I say something, you do it. We're a good team, whatever anyone says.
I've never had to tell you twice. Well. Rarely.
Advice given, advice taken. The page is tidy.
You make being right feel almost useful.
Between us, we're nearly sensible.

rules.note: Pinned with a maximum so the week line stops being true at a month and shouting over the month one.
rules.about: Now and then after your first week together, until a month. {days} is how many days.
say: A week and counting, you and me. Settling in nicely.
{days} days I've been following you about. Nothing to report.
Past the first week. The notes are getting personal.
{days} days. Long enough to learn your walk.
A month and more of this. I'd not have guessed it would stick.
{days} days. Not that I keep a calendar. I keep a calendar.
A month, give or take. Mostly give.
{days} days in. The early pages already read like history.
{days} days I've known you. That's a proper stretch, that is.
Over a hundred days. I've seen you at your best and the other thing.
{days} days. The notebook needed a second volume.
A hundred days and more. You've not got rid of me yet.

rules.note: The one that could not exist without a date. A session count can say a hundred logins; only a calendar can say a year, and they are different claims about a friendship.
rules.about: Now and then once you have known each other a year. {days} is how many days.
say: Over a year, this. {days} days. I looked it up.
A year of walking behind you. I'd do it again.
{days} days. I'm not going anywhere, in case that was in doubt.
{days} days, and I could still tell you about day one.
A year and more. The spine's cracked on this volume.

rules.note: The same day of the year as the first one, the first year only: every line says a year. Priority high enough to beat the everyday chatter, because it happens once.
rules.about: A year to the day since you first met.
say: It's today, you know. A year since we first met. I remembered.
A year ago today. Same face, better hat.
Happy anniversary. I'll not make a fuss. That was the fuss.
I wrote the date down the day we met. Today it's a year.
Today's the day, a year on. No fuss, just the one line in the book.

rules.note: Drawn from whichever tally is highest, so it moves as your play moves, and said only once the player has AGREED to it through the ask-nickname question. The names live at the top of this file, not in the code.
rules.about: Now and then uses the nickname you agreed to. {nickname} is the name.
say: All right, {nickname}.
I've got you filed under {nickname}. It fits.
If anyone reads these notes, they'll know you as {nickname}.
It's official. The index says {nickname}.
History gets a say, and it says {nickname}.
{nickname}. Cross-referenced and everything.

rules.note: The earned name, proposed rather than used. The overhead line says the candidate; the tree in dialogs.json asks whether the player minds, and only a yes makes it the nickname the other lines say. A no is remembered and that name is never offered again. Every asks rule needs the none/asking guard.
rules.about: Suggests a nickname for you. Talk to it to say yes or no. {candidate} is the name.
say: I've been calling you {candidate} in the notes. Do you mind?
In the index you're down as {candidate}. Talk to me if you object.
I'm thinking of filing you under {candidate}. Tell me if you mind.

rules.note: A yes to the nickname question. The name is settled before this fires, so {nickname} is the one just agreed.
rules.about: When you say yes to the nickname. {nickname} is the name.
say: {nickname} it is. Underlined.
Good. {nickname} goes on the spine.
Then that's settled. {nickname}.

rules.note: A no to the nickname question. Struck through and never offered again; a different name earned later is asked about afresh.
rules.about: When you say no to the nickname. That name is never offered again.
say: Fair enough. Struck through.
Then it stays off the record. I'll think of another.
Right. Back to your proper name in the file, then.

rules.note: Ask me later. The candidate stays a candidate and the question comes round again after its cooldown.
rules.about: When you ask it to suggest the nickname another time.
say: In pencil, then.
I'll ask again. Patience is most of the job.
Later it is. The index can wait.

rules.note: The greeting with the agreed name in it, some of the time. Outranks the plain greeting by one; the chance roll keeps that one in play.
rules.about: A hello with your nickname in it, some of the time.
say: Hello, {nickname}. I've saved you a fresh page.
{nickname}. Back again. Good.
Ah, {nickname}. I was hoping it'd be you.
The file says {nickname}. The file is pleased.
There's {nickname}. I'd only got as far as the date.

rules.note: The half hour after the player did what the follower asked - went where it wanted, brought what it wished for. The body pays the favour back on its own (closer attention, quicker gestures); this is the rare line that says so.
rules.about: In the half hour after you did what it asked, a rare word of thanks.
say: Still in your debt from earlier. I'm keeping a closer eye today.
I haven't forgotten the favour. You'll get my best work today.
You did the thing I asked. I've been standing a little straighter since.

rules.note: Ten times better dressed than the day it met you. Needs a first-meeting figure, so a follower that has only ever known you rich stays quiet rather than inventing a humble beginning.
rules.about: Ten times better dressed than the day it met you.
say: Look at you now. You were in rags when we met.
I remember what you turned up in. This is better.
You've come up in the world. I was there for the bottom of it.
The kit's improved beyond recognition. The walk's the same.
Page one has you in your old kit. I look at it whenever you get too grand.

rules.note: A wager on YOU rather than on the world. Guarded against a second one and against talking over a piece of advice still outstanding.
rules.about: Sometimes during a fight, it bets you cannot get ten kills in five minutes.
say: Ten of them. Five minutes. I say you can't.
Right, a wager. Ten kills before I lose interest. Go on.
Bet you can't manage ten in five minutes. Prove me wrong.
Let's have a little bet. Ten before five minutes are up.
I've set a mark. Ten of them, five minutes. Impress me.
Care to make this interesting? Ten kills. Clock's running.

rules.note: Paid out. Above the kill rules so the wager beats the cheer.
rules.about: When you win its wager. {challenge} is what it bet you could not do.
say: You did it, {challenge} with time to spare.
All right, that was impressive. I'll say it once.
Done, and I'm out of pocket. Worth it.
That's ten. I'll have to expect more of you now.
Well. That's me told.
Paid in full. That's a win for you in the book.
Time. You didn't get there.
That's five minutes. I win, and I'm insufferable about it.
Time, I'm afraid. Closer than I expected, mind.
Short of the mark. I'll try not to bring it up.
Time's up. You've lost the bet, but not your dignity.
Not this time. We'll call it a near thing.

rules.note: The one ordinary nuisance of a companion that nothing acknowledged. Short lines: it is an interruption, and a paragraph would be worse than the standing there.
rules.about: When it ends up standing in your way.
say: In your way, am I? Moving.
Right, that's me in the way again.
Excuse me. I'll just get out of your way.
I was standing there. I'm aware.
My fault. Shifting.
And there I am, underfoot again.
You walk, I dodge. That's the system.
One of us has to give way. It's me. It's always me.

rules.note: Not the same as idle, which a player working a furnace also satisfies. The camera is the tell: it moves when somebody is there.
rules.about: Now and then when you seem to have stepped away from the game.
say: You've gone, haven't you.
I'll talk amongst myself, then.
Kettle on, is it? Take your time.
Nobody's driving. I'll keep an eye on things.
Off making tea, I expect. Reasonable.
Gone quiet up there. I'll mind the shop.
I'll use the time to tidy my notes. They're immaculate.
Still gone. The scenery's had my full attention.
The notes on your absence are brief so far.
Nothing's happened. I've got it down in some detail.
Two of us here, if you count the notebook.
Gone long enough to be a paragraph.
Wherever you've gone, I hope it's well documented.
I'll pretend that was a dramatic pause.
You've left me in charge. I've told the birds.
I'll add you to the list of things not currently here.
That's another quiet page. They're my favourite.
Nobody to follow for now. I'll stand somewhere sensible.
I was saying something. It'll keep.
There'll be a summary. It's one word.
I do some of my best noticing alone.

rules.note: A world hop landed. The one thing that actually changed is everyone; the scenery came along.
rules.about: When you hop worlds. {world} is the new world.
say: Same field, different census.
World {world}. The scenery didn't even blink.
Everyone's been replaced. I'll pretend not to notice.
A new world. The roads, I note, came with us.
World {world}. I'll start the head count again.

rules.note: First login on a new game build - the world literally changes weekly, and a keeper of maps would notice. Delay puts it after the greeting.
rules.about: Your first login after a game update.
say: The world moved in the night. I'll have to redraw the maps.
They've changed the world again. Nobody consulted the scribe.
Something's shifted since we were last out. I'll re-survey as we go.

rules.note: phrases.json changed on disk and hot-reloaded. In-world, somebody wrote in the scribe's own book. Long cooldown so an editing session earns one remark.
rules.about: When you save changes to its lines in this window.
say: This isn't my handwriting.
Someone's been in my notes. The margins are different.
The annotations are an improvement. Worrying.
My notebook smells of fresh ink I didn't buy.

rules.note: A music track unlocked - somewhere new enough to have its own song. The tally 'music' counts unlocks since install.
rules.about: When you unlock a music track. {track} is the track.
say: Another one for the catalogue: {track}.
{track}. Must be somewhere new, if it's got its own song.
New tune. {track}, the locals call it.

rules.note: The fiftieth track unlocked since the follower arrived. Exact tally bracket so it says this once, on the moment.
rules.about: The fiftieth music track unlocked since you met.
say: Fifty songs since we met. The catalogue wants a second volume.

rules.note: A boss's chronicle page was just written, the first time the scribe set eyes on it. The plugin holds the news until the follower has the floor, so it comes after the boss's own line rather than into it.
rules.about: When a boss earns a page in the Chronicle, the first time it sees one. {page} is the page.
say: {page} goes in the book. I'll write it up from further away.
{page}, written up. The handwriting's a bit shaky.
A page for {page}. I'll want the good ink for this one.

rules.note: A creature's chronicle page was just written, the first time one came into view. Held until the follower has the floor.
rules.about: When a creature earns a page in the Chronicle, the first time it sees one. {page} is the page.
say: Got a good look at that one. It goes in under {page}.
{page}. I'll be writing that one up, and I won't be kind.
I saw one myself. That's how a page should start.

rules.note: A place's chronicle page was just written, the first time you walked into it. Held until the follower has the floor, so the arrival line goes first. Its sketch comes later, when you pose for it there.
rules.about: When a place gets a page in the Chronicle, the first time you walk in. {page} is the page.
say: {page} has a page now. Find me a good spot and pose for me.
Starting a page on {page}. I've got the name down, at least.
New page for {page}. I'll write it up once I've had a look round.

rules.note: A faction or world page was just written by walking into its land. Pages a quest opens come as 'quest' instead.
rules.about: When a faction or world page is written as you walk into its land. {page} is the page.
say: {page}. That gets a page, and a careful one.
A page for {page}. I'll keep my voice down.

rules.note: A quest begun or finished opened a chronicle page: the quest's own page, or a place, creature or history it introduces. Nothing has been seen yet, so these claim no sighting and promise no sketch. A quest can open several pages at once; the cooldown lets one line speak for them.
rules.about: When a quest you start or finish opens a page in the Chronicle. {page} is the page.
say: That's {page} in the book. I'll write it up properly tonight.
{page} has its own page now. I'll do it justice.
I've opened a page on {page}. The ink's still wet.

rules.note: A new collection log entry - the OTHER ledger, the bank-rival canon's cousin. Only fires when the game's own log notification setting is on.
rules.about: A new collection log item. Needs the game's collection log notifications on. {item} is the item.
say: {item}, logged twice. Mine's the better ledger.
The {item} in your list. The moment in mine.
That's the {item} in both our archives now.

rules.note: The quest reward scroll - the one moment the game hands the player literal paperwork, witnessed by a professional. Tally 'quests' counts them.
rules.about: When you complete a quest. {quest} is the quest.
say: {quest}, done and witnessed. A full page.
{quest}. Nice scroll. Mine has footnotes.
{quest}. Signed, sealed, filed.
Finished. Let me see the scroll before you put it away.

rules.note: The tenth quest completed since the follower arrived. Exact bracket, once.
rules.about: The tenth quest you complete since you met.
say: Ten quests since we met. The index has its own page now.

rules.note: A Grand Exchange buy completed, often miles from the Exchange - the clerk receives the telegram wherever you are.
rules.about: When a Grand Exchange buy completes, wherever you are. {item} is the item.
say: Bought the {item}. The ledger balances.
Word's come through. You've got the {item}.
Your {item} arrived. I signed for it in spirit.

rules.note: A Grand Exchange sale completed. The estate grows; the scribe approves of liquidation on principle.
rules.about: When a Grand Exchange sale completes. {item} is the item and {value} the price.
say: Sold the {item}. That's {value} to the estate.
The {item} went. Try to look like you'll miss it.
Your {item} sold. The economy thanks you.

rules.note: Somebody arrived in the friends chat or clan channel. Low duty cycle on purpose: a busy clan should be a murmur, not a roll call.
rules.about: Sometimes when someone joins your friends chat or clan channel. {name} is who.
say: {name}'s turned up. I'll mark them present.
There's {name}. I'll take the register.
{name}'s in. I'll give them a line in the book.
{name} has arrived. Noted, with the time.

rules.note: Somebody left the channel. The drier entry of the two.
rules.about: Sometimes when someone leaves the channel. {name} is who.
say: There goes {name}. The minutes will show it.
{name}'s gone. Fewer witnesses.
{name} has left. I've put the time down, in case it matters.

rules.title: Someone shouting nearby
rules.note: Any named NPC shouting overhead nearby - the town crier, a quest scene, a market stall. Heavy chance gate: busy scenes shout constantly.
rules.about: Now and then, when someone nearby shouts something. {npc} is who.
say: I wrote down what {npc} said. Most of it.
I heard you, {npc}. So did everybody.
{npc} wants that on the record. It very nearly is.

rules.note: The first of every month, on the player's own calendar - day without month means every month. The scribe's favourite day.
rules.about: The first of every month, by your own calendar.
say: New month. Fresh page. Let's fill this one with better decisions.
First of the month. I've ruled the columns already.
A new month. The old one's filed under done.

rules.note: The 24th through the 26th of December, player's own calendar. Once per session at most; the cooldown keeps a relog from repeating it same day.
rules.about: From 24 to 26 December, by your own calendar. Once a session at most.
say: Christmas. I got you nothing. I wrote you in, though.
Merry Christmas. The ledger takes the day off. I don't.

rules.note: New Year's Eve into New Year's Day, wrapping past the year end the way the late-night clock window wraps past midnight.
rules.about: New Year's Eve and New Year's Day, by your own calendar.
say: A new year. Next volume, same author.
The year's turning. I'll be mis-dating entries for a month.

rules.note: The 31st of October. The scarecrow canon gets its day.
rules.about: On 31 October, by your own calendar.
say: All Hallows. Every scarecrow tonight is a suspect.
Halloween. If the graveyard moves, I'm not recording it.

rules.note: The one track name certain enough to write a rule for. musicTrack fires on the change TO a track; users add their own opinions in the editor.
rules.about: When Sea Shanty 2 starts playing.
say: Sea Shanty 2. The sailors request it nightly. The sailors are the problem.
This tune again. I've transcribed it. It doesn't help.

rules.note: The player examined something and the follower turned to look at it too. The head-turn is the usual whole reaction; this line is the garnish. Examining is player-INITIATED - they are asking for attention - so it answers readily, but not every single time.
rules.about: When you examine something, it looks too, and often has a word. {target} is the thing.
say: One {target}. Fair condition, I'd say.
The {target}. I'll note it, if I must.
I wrote up the {target} once. Not my best work.
The {target} as well? We're being thorough today.
Ah, the {target}. I have opinions.
{target}. Write it down, we might be tested.
You looked, so I looked. Teamwork.
Is the {target} interesting? Be honest.
A {target}, apparently. The description insists.
I'd have guessed a {target} without reading it.
Another {target} for the looked-at pile.
The {target}. Riveting stuff.
The {target}: noted, filed, forgotten by lunch.
Looking closely at the {target}, are we?
A {target}. I'd hoped for more, honestly.
Someone worked hard describing the {target}.
{target}. There. Now we both know.
The {target}. Yes. Very much so.
Careful! Oh, it's only a {target}. Carry on.
One more {target} and it's going in the notebook.
You really do read everything, don't you?
Go on then. What did it say?
I looked where you looked. I saw a {target}.
You do like reading the small print.

rules.note: The follower just minuted one of the player's NPC dialogs - stepped aside, wrote through the meeting, put the scroll away as the box closed. The performance is the joke; the line is the rare receipt.
rules.about: Sometimes, after it has taken notes during a conversation of yours.
say: I have the minutes, if it ever comes to a dispute.
I've minuted every word of that. Some of the pauses, too.
That's in the record now. They seemed nice.

rules.note: The player came back from a long AFK during which the follower walked round to peer at them. The check itself was silent (the damper held); this is the payoff, on a present player.
rules.about: Back from a long spell away from the keyboard, after it came round to check on you.
say: Back with us. You had the look of somebody listening at a door.
There you are. I came round to check, and you hadn't moved an inch.
Welcome back. You passed your welfare check, barely.

rules.title: Lumbridge, after Cook's Assistant
rules.note: Callback: stands in for area-lumbridge on about 35% of arrivals once Cook's Assistant is done, at most every 30 minutes; the base's lines play the rest of the time.
rules.about: Now and then on arriving in Lumbridge, once Cook's Assistant is done.
say: The cook's still telling people about that cake.
The Duke got his cake. I'm still waiting on my party invitation.

rules.title: Lumbridge, after Sheep Shearer
rules.note: Callback: stands in for area-lumbridge on about 30% of arrivals once Sheep Shearer is done, at most every 30 minutes; the base's lines play the rest of the time.
rules.about: Now and then on arriving in Lumbridge, once Sheep Shearer is done.
say: I still can't pass a spinning wheel without counting to twenty.
The sheep round here give us a look now. Word's got about.

rules.title: Paterdomus, after Priest in Peril
rules.note: New place line with no base rule: only exists once Priest in Peril is done. About 50% of arrivals, at most every 30 minutes.
rules.about: Now and then on arriving in Paterdomus, once Priest in Peril is done.
say: Paterdomus. I say a quiet word for the dog every time we cross.
The temple again. I give the coffins outside a very wide berth.

rules.title: Baxtorian Falls, after Waterfall Quest
rules.note: New place line with no base rule: only exists once Waterfall Quest is done. About 50% of arrivals, at most every 30 minutes.
rules.about: Now and then on arriving in Baxtorian Falls, once Waterfall Quest is done.
say: The falls sound different now I know what's behind them.
Hudon's still out on that rock, I expect. His mother has my sympathy.

rules.title: Varrock, after Children of the Sun
rules.note: Callback: stands in for area-varrock on about 25% of arrivals once Children of the Sun is done, at most every 40 minutes; the base's lines play the rest of the time.
rules.about: Now and then on arriving in Varrock, once Children of the Sun is done.
say: Varrock. I still give every guard's uniform a second look.
Any guard here carrying a large bag gets watched. I learned that much.

rules.title: Taverley, after Witch's House
rules.note: Callback: stands in for area-taverley on about 35% of arrivals once Witch's House is done, at most every 30 minutes; the base's lines play the rest of the time.
rules.about: Now and then on arriving in Taverley, once Witch's House is done.
say: Taverley. I keep to the far side of the witch's hedge.
If that boy's ball goes over again, he can knock on her door himself.

rules.title: Draynor Village, after X Marks the Spot
rules.note: Callback: stands in for area-draynor on about 35% of arrivals once X Marks the Spot is done, at most every 30 minutes; the base's lines play the rest of the time.
rules.about: Now and then on arriving in Draynor Village, once X Marks the Spot is done.
say: Every pig pen I pass, I listen. Draynor's has kept quiet since.
Two of Veos' holes were round here, and I still don't know what he got.

rules.title: Crandor, after Dragon Slayer I
rules.note: Callback: stands in for area-crandor on about 60% of arrivals once Dragon Slayer I is done, at most every 30 minutes; the base's lines play the rest of the time.
rules.about: Now and then on arriving in Crandor, once Dragon Slayer I is done.
say: Crandor, with no dragon on it. The island looks almost relieved.
Elvarg's island. I still check the sky, out of respect.

rules.title: The Wizards' Tower, after Rune Mysteries
rules.note: New place line with no base rule: only exists once Rune Mysteries is done. About 50% of arrivals, at most every 30 minutes.
rules.about: Now and then on arriving in the Wizards' Tower, once Rune Mysteries is done.
say: Sedridor's basement is under us. I'm still working out how he knew you.
Someone in the Wizards' Tower knows your name. I keep mine quiet.
Somebody in that tower knows your name. I keep mine quiet here.

rules.title: Piscarilius, after Client of Kourend
rules.note: Callback: stands in for area-piscarilius on about 35% of arrivals once Client of Kourend is done, at most every 30 minutes; the base's lines play the rest of the time.
rules.about: Now and then on arriving in Piscarilius, once Client of Kourend is done.
say: Don't ask Veos about the client. He doesn't remember any of it, and I do.
Port Piscarilius. If Veos asks, we never met the client.

rules.title: Duke Horacio, after Cook's Assistant
rules.note: Callback: same trigger as quest-duke-horacio plus Cook's Assistant done, one point higher, cooldown three times the base's. First meeting after the quest gets this; while it cools down the base wins. Not a hand-in NPC for Cook's Assistant, so it cannot rise on the quest finishing.
rules.about: Now and then when Duke Horacio is near, once Cook's Assistant is done.
say: He had his cake, and never once asked who fetched the flour.
The Duke looks well. Cake will do that.

rules.title: Duke Horacio, after Rune Mysteries
rules.note: Callback: same trigger as quest-duke-horacio plus Rune Mysteries done, one point higher, cooldown three times the base's. First meeting after the quest gets this; while it cools down the base wins. Not a hand-in NPC for Rune Mysteries, so it cannot rise on the quest finishing.
rules.about: Now and then when Duke Horacio is near, once Rune Mysteries is done.
say: If the Duke's found anything else in that cellar, I'm not carrying it.
The Duke. If he finds another talisman, he can deliver it himself.

rules.title: King Roald, after Priest in Peril
rules.note: Callback: same trigger as quest-king-roald plus Priest in Peril done, one point higher, cooldown three times the base's. First meeting after the quest gets this; while it cools down the base wins. Not a hand-in NPC for Priest in Peril, so it cannot rise on the quest finishing.
rules.about: Now and then when King Roald is near, once Priest in Peril is done.
say: He's not mentioned the dog since. I've chosen to call that forgiveness.
The King. I'd keep the conversation well away from dogs.

rules.title: Sergeant Tobyn, after Children of the Sun
rules.note: Callback: same trigger as quest-sergeant-tobyn plus Children of the Sun seen done a day or more before, one point higher, cooldown three times the base's. First meeting after the quest gets this; while it cools down the base wins. Roof Tobyn (6781, shown as 12648 at varbit 9632 = 16-24) stays after the quest, whose end state is 24 (cache; Quest Helper ChildrenOfTheSun); Alina and Noah, its first target, are gone from 7 on. He stands by as the quest ends, so the day's wait keeps it from rising then.
rules.about: Now and then when Sergeant Tobyn is near, once Children of the Sun is done.
say: Tobyn's still minding his bandit. That report must be a long one by now.
Noah saw that bag before any of us. I hope somebody thanked him.

rules.title: Aubury, after Rune Mysteries
rules.note: Callback: same trigger as quest-aubury plus Rune Mysteries done, one point higher, cooldown three times the base's. First meeting after the quest gets this; while it cools down the base wins. Not a hand-in NPC for Rune Mysteries, so it cannot rise on the quest finishing.
rules.about: Now and then when Aubury is near, once Rune Mysteries is done.
say: Aubury. He still checks our hands for packages when we walk in.
Aubury. I'd still like to know what was in those notes.

rules.title: Father Aereck, after The Restless Ghost
rules.note: Callback: same trigger as quest-father-aereck plus The Restless Ghost done, one point higher, cooldown three times the base's. First meeting after the quest gets this; while it cools down the base wins. Not a hand-in NPC for The Restless Ghost, so it cannot rise on the quest finishing.
rules.about: Now and then when Father Aereck is near, once The Restless Ghost is done.
say: Father Aereck. One fewer ghost in his graveyard, thanks to you.
The ghost's at rest. Father Aereck could do with some of that himself.

rules.title: Ned, after Dragon Slayer I
rules.note: Callback: same trigger as quest-ned plus Dragon Slayer I done, one point higher, cooldown three times the base's. First meeting after the quest gets this; while it cools down the base wins. Not a hand-in NPC for Dragon Slayer I, so it cannot rise on the quest finishing.
rules.about: Now and then when Ned is near, once Dragon Slayer I is done.
say: Ned did get us to Crandor. I've stopped arguing about the word captain.
The boat's still in bits on Crandor. Ned's never once brought it up.

rules.title: Regath, after Client of Kourend
rules.note: Callback: same trigger as quest-regath plus Client of Kourend done, one point higher, cooldown three times the base's. First meeting after the quest gets this; while it cools down the base wins. Not a hand-in NPC for Client of Kourend, so it cannot rise on the quest finishing.
rules.about: Now and then when Regath is near, once Client of Kourend is done.
say: Regath still thinks you're a journalist. He's never seen your writing.

rules.title: Leenz, after Client of Kourend
